If you are wondering what to do in Recife this weekend, you have picked a good one, because Saturday 15. Sunday 16 and Monday 17 August 2026 are packed with the kind of events Pernambuco does best.

A big free forró concert doubles as a DVD taping across the water in Olinda, a ten-day circus festival opens for free in a city park. A fair of Black-owned businesses is on at the mall, and theaters around Greater Recife are full.

We have pulled together the confirmed events, with dates, venues and exactly what you will pay. So you can plan before the days fill up.

A weekend built around forró, circus and ciranda

The best news is that many of this weekend’s highlights are completely free. The headline forró show, the whole circus festival and the Black-owned business fair all cost nothing to attend.

So you can have a full weekend without spending much at all. The action is spread across Greater Recife, the metropolitan region that includes Recife itself, neighboring Olinda and Jaboatão dos Guararapes.

However, distances are short, and the neighborhoods of Pina. Boa Viagem and the old port district of Bairro do Recife hold most of what is on.

Below we run through the free forró taping first, then explain forró for anyone new to it. Cover the circus festival and the mall fair, a Monday wellness talk.

The theater on offer, and finish with getting-around and cost tips.

Raí Saia Rodada records a free anniversary DVD in Olinda

The single biggest free plan is on Sunday 16 August. The band Raí Saia Rodada marks 25 years on the road by recording a live DVD.

And the whole thing is open to the public at no charge. It happens from 4pm in the external area of the Centro de Convenções de Pernambuco.

On Avenida Professor Andrade Bezerra in the Salgadinho district of Olinda, just over the boundary from Recife. Since it is an outdoor stage with a large crowd expected, arrive early.

Entry is free, but there is a catch worth knowing: you need to reserve a ticket online through the Evenyx platform. Limited to two per CPF (the Brazilian tax ID), and bring 2kg of non-perishable food to donate at the gate.

Guest performers announced include Joelma, Wesley Safadão and Natanzinho Lima, so the line-up runs well beyond the host band.

What is forró, and who is Raí Saia Rodada?

If you are new to the Northeast, forró is the music and dance that defines it. It is upbeat, accordion-driven party music, traditionally built around three instruments, the accordion.

The zabumba drum and the triangle, and it is danced in close pairs with a quick, shuffling step. In Pernambuco it is the sound of family parties, bars and the huge June festivals.

Raí Saia Rodada is one of the most popular acts in the more modern. Electric style known as forró eletrônico, with a quarter-century of hits behind them.

A DVD taping like this one is a big deal locally: it is part concert. Part recording session, with a bigger production and more guest stars than a normal show.

You do not need to know a single song to enjoy it. Just turn up, expect a warm and busy crowd, and let the rhythm do the rest.

It is one of the most authentic nights out you can have in the region, and this one happens to be free.

The 15th Recife Circus Festival takes over the city

The 15th edition of the Recife Circus Festival, known locally as the Mostra de Circo do Recife. Opens on Saturday 15 August and runs for ten days, through to Tuesday 25 August.

With shows, workshops and tributes at venues across the city. The opening is on Saturday 15 August at Parque Governador Eduardo Campos.

In the Pina district near the Via Mangue, with an open ‘Ocupa Circo’ takeover from 4pm to 7pm. There are hands-on circus sessions with local companies, a showcase of short acts, and a headline performance to close the afternoon.

In addition, everything at the festival is free to attend. Which makes it an easy plan for families or anyone curious about Brazilian circus arts.

Before you go, check the daily program, as the line-up moves around the city over the ten days.

Expo Preta and the ciranda queen at RioMar

Over at RioMar Recife, the big shopping mall in Pina at Avenida República do Líbano 251. The 5th Expo Preta runs through Sunday 16 August.

It is a fair of Black-owned Pernambuco businesses, with around 20 brands selling fashion, beauty, art, food, plants and crafts. Entry is free.

The fair sits on the Praça de Eventos on floor L1 and follows mall hours: 9am to 10pm on Saturday and 12pm to 9pm on Sunday. It is an easy, air-conditioned browse if the heat gets much, and a good way to support small local makers.

The fair opened on Thursday 13 August with a ciranda concert by Lia de Itamaracá at the mall’s Teatro RioMar. If you have not heard of her, she is the ‘Rainha da Ciranda’, the queen of ciranda.

A slow, circular dance from the coast of Pernambuco performed hand in hand in a big ring. Now in her eighties and officially recognized as a Living Heritage of Pernambuco.

She is one of the great voices of the state. That opening show has passed, but the fair itself is open all weekend.

Monja Coen and a wellness week on Monday

If you are around on Monday 17 August, there is a standout talk to catch. The Zen Buddhist monk Monja Coen, one of Brazil’s best-known spiritual teachers.

Gives a lecture titled ‘Mente Próspera: A Vida é Aqui e Agora’ (‘A Prosperous Mind: Life Is Here and Now’). It is at 7pm at the Teatro RioMar, inside the same RioMar Recife mall in Pina.

As part of the venue’s ‘Semana RioMar de Bem com a Vida’ wellness week running 15 to 20 August. Tickets are R$40 full price and R$20 half price (about US$8 and US$4).

Sold through the RioMar Recife app and the theater box office. The talk is in Portuguese, so a little of the language helps.

Theater across Greater Recife this weekend

Recife’s stages are busy this weekend, with plays for a range of budgets. The headline is ‘O Estrangeiro – Versão Multimídia’, a multimedia take on Albert Camus, at the Teatro Luiz Mendonça in Parque Dona Lindu.

Boa Viagem, on Saturday 15 August at 8pm and Sunday 16 August at 6pm. Tickets are R$65 half price and R$130 full (about US$13 and US$25), sold through the INTI platform.

For something more intimate, ‘Pela Noite’, marking 30 years without the writer Caio Fernando Abreu. Plays the Teatro Hermilo Borba Filho at Cais do Apolo 142 in the old port district on Saturday 15 August at 6pm and Sunday 16 August at 5pm.

At R$70 full and R$35 half (about US$13 and US$7). On a budget, ‘A Receita’ at Espaço O Poste on Rua do Riachuelo 641 in Boa Vista runs Saturday 15 August at 7pm for a flat R$10 (about US$2), and ‘Diatribe de Amor’.

From a text by Gabriel García Márquez, plays the CAIXA Cultural Recife on Saturday 15 August at 4pm and 7:30pm. At R$30 full and R$15 half (about US$6 and US$3), sold through Sympla.

More free circus on Sunday

Beyond the main festival, there is a lovely free circus show on Sunday 16 August. ‘Circo Godot’ plays the auditorium of the Museu Cais do Sertão, in the Bairro do Recife port district, at 5pm.

Entry is free, it is suitable for all ages, and it comes with audio description for visually impaired audiences. While you are there, the museum itself is worth a look, sitting right on the old waterfront.

Pairing the museum, the circus show and a wander around the restored streets of the old port makes for an easy. Low-cost Sunday afternoon in the heart of the city.

Getting around and where to base yourself

Greater Recife is spread out, so plan your trips. Boa Viagem is the main beach neighborhood where most visitors and many expats stay, with hotels.

Restaurants and an easy walk to the Teatro Luiz Mendonça in Parque Dona Lindu. The old port district, Bairro do Recife.

Holds the Museu Cais do Sertão and several theaters and is best reached by taxi or ride-hailing app, especially at night. Pina, home to RioMar Recife and the circus festival’s opening park, sits between the two.

The Sunday forró taping is across the water in Salgadinho, Olinda, which is a short ride from central Recife. Ride-hailing apps work well across the region, but fares climb when a big event lets out.

So build that into your budget for the Saia Rodada night.

What it costs and practical tips

The value play this weekend is to lean on the free events: the Saia Rodada DVD taping. The entire circus festival, the Expo Preta fair and the Sunday ‘Circo Godot’ show all cost nothing to attend.

For the free forró show, sort your Evenyx ticket in advance and buy your 2kg of donation food before you go. As gate queues can be long.

Carry a little cash for the fair’s smaller stalls and for street snacks, even though malls and official ticket sites take cards. Finally, if you are still deciding what to do in Recife this weekend.

The two easiest all-day plans are the free circus opening on Saturday in Pina and the free forró taping on Sunday in Olinda. All prices here are converted at 1 US dollar to 5.19 reais, the rate on 14 August 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What free things can I do in Recife this weekend?

Plenty. Raí Saia Rodada’s 25-year anniversary DVD taping is free on Sunday 16 August from 4pm at the Centro de Convenções in Olinda (reserve on Evenyx and bring 2kg of food to donate).

How do I get tickets for the Raí Saia Rodada show?

The Sunday 16 August DVD taping is free, but you must reserve a ticket online through the Evenyx platform. Limited to two per CPF, and bring 2kg of non-perishable food to donate at the entrance.

How much are theater tickets in Recife this weekend?

They vary widely. ‘O Estrangeiro’ at the Teatro Luiz Mendonça is R$65 to R$130 (about US$13 to US$25).

When is the Recife Circus Festival and is it free?

The 15th Recife Circus Festival (Mostra de Circo do Recife) runs ten days. From Saturday 15 August to Tuesday 25 August 2026, at venues across the city.

World.title: Buenos Aires Long Weekend: Shows, Gastronomy and Culture, August 15-17
World.content:
Argentina · Weekend

Key Facts — When Saturday 15, Sunday 16 and Monday 17 August 2026; Monday is the Paso a la Inmortalidad del General San Martin holiday, so it is a three-day long weekend.

— Big shows Soda Stereo’s ‘Ecos’ plays Movistar Arena on Saturday 15 August (from ARS 70,000, about US$47), Ruben Blades on Sunday 16 August (from ARS 45,000, about US$30) and La Konga on Monday 17 August (from ARS 55,000, about US$37).

— High culture Verdi’s opera ‘Otello’ runs at the Teatro Colon on Saturday 15 August at 8:00pm and Sunday 16 August at 5:00pm; tickets through the theatre’s own box office and website.

— Free The Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes is free and open Saturday and Sunday 10:00am-8:00pm; the San Telmo Sunday fair and the Feria de Mataderos (Sunday and the Monday holiday) are free too.

— Exchange rate Prices converted at about 1 USD = 1,500 ARS (mid-August 2026; official rate near ARS 1,465 and the parallel rate near ARS 1,521 on 11 August).

With Monday’s San Martin holiday turning three days free, the city hands you arena concerts, a Verdi opera. Free museums and Sunday fairs where you can eat your way through the barrios.

The Teatro Colon in Buenos Aires, which stages Verdi’s ‘Otello’ over the long weekend of 15-17 August 2026. Illustrative photo. (Photo: Andrzej Otrebski, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.)

If you are in town for the Buenos Aires long weekend, you have landed on a good one. Because Monday 17 August 2026 is the Paso a la Inmortalidad del General San Martin holiday.

Which turns Saturday 15 to Monday 17 into three full days off. That extra day gives you room to mix a big arena concert with a night at the opera.

A wander through free museums and a lazy Sunday of street fairs and regional food. We have pulled together the events we could confirm, with dates.

Venues and what you will actually pay, so you can plan before the city fills up.

Planning your Buenos Aires long weekend

The holiday on Monday marks the anniversary of the death of General Jose de San Martin. The soldier who led Argentina, Chile and Peru to independence.

It is a moveable feriado fixed to the third Monday of August. And in 2026 that lands on the 17th, giving locals and expats alike a proper three-day break.

The nice thing about this particular weekend is how much of it is free or cheap. You can happily fill all three days on a small budget, then splurge on one big night if you fancy it.

Most of what follows sits within the city itself, easy to reach on the Subte or a short taxi ride. Below we run through the headline concerts first, then the opera, the museums.

And the Sunday and holiday fairs where the food is, followed by a few practical tips on tickets, money and getting around.

Three big nights at Movistar Arena

The anchor of the weekend is Movistar Arena, the city’s main indoor venue, at Humboldt 450 in the Villa Crespo neighbourhood. It has a different headliner on each of the three nights.

So there is a good chance one of them is your thing. On Saturday 15 August, Soda Stereo return with their ‘Ecos’ production, the tribute show built around the band’s classic catalogue.

Tickets start at around ARS 70,000, roughly US$47. On Sunday 16 August, the Panamanian legend Ruben Blades brings his ‘Fotografias’ tour, with tickets from about ARS 45,000, or US$30.

The holiday Monday, 17 August, belongs to La Konga, the cuarteto act that has become one of the country’s biggest live draws. With seats from around ARS 55,000, about US$37.

Buy through the official Movistar Arena website rather than resellers, and note that prices rise as the cheaper sections sell out.

A night at the opera: Verdi’s Otello

If you would rather dress up for something grand, the Teatro Colon is staging Giuseppe Verdi’s ‘Otello’ over the weekend. The opera house, at Cerrito 628 in the Microcentro, is one of the great theatres of the world.

And worth the visit for the building alone. There are two performances in your window: Saturday 15 August at 8:00pm and Sunday 16 August at 5:00pm.

With more dates running later in the month. Ticket prices vary widely by seating section, from affordable upper-gallery seats to pricey stalls, so check the current bands when you book.

Tickets are sold through the Teatro Colon’s own box office and official website. If the opera itself feels like a stretch.

The theatre also runs guided tours most days, a lovely lower-commitment way to see inside.

Free and low-cost museums

Museums are where the long weekend gets cheap. The Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, the national fine-arts museum at Av.

del Libertador 1473 in Recoleta, is free to enter, with donations welcome. It opens Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August from 10:00am to 8:00pm.

One catch worth planning around: Bellas Artes closes every Monday, holiday or not, so it will be shut on Monday 17. Do that visit on the Saturday or Sunday instead.

For contemporary and Latin American art, MALBA in Palermo, at Av. Figueroa Alcorta 3415, stays open right through the long weekend, Thursday to Monday from noon to 8:00pm, including the holiday.

General admission is about ARS 12,000 (US$8), with a reduced ARS 6,000 (US$4) for students. Teachers and retirees, and free entry for young children.

Sunday fairs and where to eat

Sunday is fair day in Buenos Aires. In the cobbled heart of San Telmo, the weekly Feria de San Telmo spreads antiques.

Crafts and food stalls along Calle Defensa and around Plaza Dorrego from about 10:00am to 5:00pm. It is free to wander, and the surrounding cafes and parrillas are a fine place to graze.

Further out, the Feria de Mataderos is the one to seek out for regional cooking and folk culture. Held opposite the old livestock market in the Mataderos neighbourhood, it runs on Sundays and public holidays from 11:00am to 8:00pm.

Which means it is on both Sunday 16 and the Monday 17 holiday. This is the fair for empanadas, locro, grilled meats and dulces from around the country, with live folk music and gaucho dancing.

Entry is free; you simply pay for what you eat and drink. Which makes it an easy, low-cost plan for a slow afternoon.

Tickets, timings and how to buy

For the arena shows, buy directly from the Movistar Arena website. The Teatro Colon sells its opera tickets through its own site and box office.

Both tend to release seats in price tiers, so the earlier you book, the more of the cheaper sections are still available. For the museums and fairs you need nothing in advance.

Bellas Artes lets you walk straight in for free. While MALBA is quicker if you buy your timed ticket online before arriving, especially over a busy holiday weekend.

Doors at concerts usually open an hour or two before the billed start time. And Argentine shows often begin late, so do not panic if the room is quiet at the printed hour.

Money and getting around

A quick word on money, because Argentina has more than one exchange rate. In mid-August 2026 the official rate sat near ARS 1,465 to the US dollar and the parallel.

Or ‘blue’, rate near ARS 1,521, both quoted around 11 August. We have used a round 1 USD to 1,500 ARS for the conversions above.

So treat the dollar figures as a guide rather than a fixed price. Cards are widely accepted at big venues and museums, but the Sunday fairs run largely on cash.

So carry some pesos for empanadas and craft stalls. A rechargeable SUBE card is the cheapest way to ride the Subte and buses across the city.

One last tip: the holiday Monday is quieter than a normal weekday, with some shops and offices closed. So build your plans around the venues and fairs that we have confirmed are open.

A weekend that stretches your pesos

Add it up and the Buenos Aires long weekend gives you a genuine range: a world-class opera house, three arena headliners. Free national art and two of the city’s best-loved fairs, most of it walkable or a short ride apart.

You could spend big on a concert or coast through all three days on free museums and fair food. Either way, the extra San Martin holiday is the gift that makes it work.

So pick your one splurge and let the rest fall into place.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is 15-17 August a long weekend in Buenos Aires?

Monday 17 August 2026 is the Paso a la Inmortalidad del General San Martin. A national holiday fixed to the third Monday of August.

What free things can I do over the weekend?

The Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes in Recoleta is free and open Saturday and Sunday from 10:00am to 8:00pm. The Feria de San Telmo runs free on Sunday along Calle Defensa.

How much do the concert tickets cost?

At Movistar Arena, Soda Stereo start around ARS 70,000 (US$47) on Saturday, Ruben Blades from about ARS 45,000 (US$30) on Sunday. And La Konga from around ARS 55,000 (US$37) on the Monday holiday.

Is the Teatro Colon open that weekend?

Yes. Verdi’s opera ‘Otello’ plays on Saturday 15 August at 8:00pm and Sunday 16 August at 5:00pm.

Sources: Perplexity sonar-pro fact-check (14 August 2026); Movistar Arena (https://www.movistararena.com.ar); Teatro Colon (https://teatrocolon.org.ar); MALBA (https://malba.org.ar) and Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes; Buenos Aires city tourism (Feria de Mataderos, Plaza Dorrego); La Nacion agenda and dollar quotes for the mid-August 2026 exchange rate.

World.title: What’s On in Rio This Weekend: Kafka, Singles’ Parties and Free Fun

Brazil · Weekend

— Theatre Caio Blat’s ‘Subversão Kafka’ at Teatro Prio, Leblon; Sat 15 Aug at 8pm, Sun 16 Aug at 7pm; R$60 to R$120 (US$12 to US$23) via Sympla.

— Free Festa Agostina da Ziriguidum at the Museu da República gardens in Catete, Sat 15 and Sun 16 Aug, 9am to 6pm, free entry.

If you are wondering what’s on in Rio this weekend, you are spoiled for choice. Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August bring a buzzy Caio Blat play.

A string of Singles’ Day parties and a free Brazilian street festival right in the middle of the city. There is plenty for every budget, from a big-ticket concert to open-air fun that costs nothing.

We have pulled together the confirmed events, with dates. Venues and what you will actually pay, so you can plan before Saturday arrives.

Your Rio This Weekend at a Glance

First, the shape of the weekend. Saturday 15 August is Singles’ Day in Brazil, known locally as the Dia dos Solteiros.

So the city’s bars lean into the theme. At the same time, the theatre and concert calendar is full.

As a result, you can pair a cultural afternoon with a late night out without leaving your neighbourhood. Below we run through the highlights in order, from stage to street party to free festival.

Everything here is confirmed, with the practical details you need to book.

Caio Blat Brings Kafka to the Stage

The most talked-about opening this week is ‘Subversão Kafka’, a new adaptation of Franz Kafka’s stories. Actor and director Caio Blat stars alongside Pedro Henrique Müller.

It plays at the Teatro Prio, on Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 1110 in Leblon, inside the Jockey Club. The season runs from mid-August, so this weekend catches its opening days.

For your dates, the show is on Saturday 15 August at 8pm and Sunday 16 August at 7pm. Tickets cost R$60 to R$120, roughly US$12 to US$23.

You buy them online through Sympla or at the venue box office. Because it is a buzzy premiere, it is worth booking ahead rather than turning up on the night.

Singles’ Day Parties Across Rio This Weekend

Singles’ Day gives Rio’s nightlife an easy hook on Saturday 15 August. Local listings from O Globo’s RioShow flag a cluster of themed parties across the city.

The clearest option for visitors is Fiesta Latina ‘Chévere’ at Tau, on Avenida Nossa Senhora de Copacabana 1417 in Copacabana. It runs from 10pm on Saturday into the early hours.

Entry is free for everyone who arrives before midnight, as long as you claim a voucher on Sympla first. After that, advance tickets start at R$30 (about US$6), with a higher price at the door.

Beyond that, Baixo Gávea and Botafogo host their own Dia dos Solteiros nights. Because covers and start times vary, check Sympla or Shotgun for each party before you head out.

A Free Brazilian Street Party by the Museums

If you would rather spend nothing, the Festa Agostina da Ziriguidum is the pick of the weekend. It takes over the gardens of the Museu da República in Catete.

It runs on both Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, from 9am to 6pm each day, with free entry. Expect forró, quadrilha dancing, craft stalls and plenty of Brazilian street food.

This is a relaxed, family-friendly celebration of the August festival season. Since it is outdoors and free, it is an easy stop before an evening show.

Big-Name Concerts: Roberto Carlos and More

For a marquee night, Brazilian legend Roberto Carlos plays the Qualistage arena on Avenida Ayrton Senna 3000 in Barra da Tijuca. He performs on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, both at 8:30pm.

Tickets start from around R$210 (about US$40) and climb by seating tier. The Saturday show has been reported as sold out, so the Sunday date is your better bet.

There is more music too. Romantic star Fábio Jr. plays Espaço Hall on Saturday.

While veteran vocal group MPB4 marks its 60th anniversary with two sets at Blue Note Rio in Copacabana.

Candlelight, Exhibitions and Indoor Culture

For something calmer, the Candlelight series returns to the Museu do Amanhã at Praça Mauá. This weekend’s programmes include tributes to Coldplay, Imagine Dragons and the ‘Bridgerton’ soundtrack.

Prices vary by session and sell through the Fever platform, so check there for the show you want. Meanwhile, the Mystic Fair holistic market runs both days at Clube Monte Líbano in Lagoa.

The city’s galleries add free options. Caixa Cultural, the CCBB and other downtown spaces have exhibitions running, many of them free or low-cost.

Free by the Sea: The Copacabana Shows

The weekend also spills over from a run of free open-air concerts on Copacabana beach. The Orquestra Ouro Preto has been playing near Posto 2 with major Brazilian names.

Samuel Rosa performed on Friday 14 August. And Alceu Valença closes the run on Saturday 15 August, both free and open to all.

We covered the full line-up separately, linked below. If you are near Copacabana on Saturday evening, it is worth wandering down to the sand.

Because there are no tickets, you simply turn up and find a spot.

Getting Around and Paying Your Way

Most of these venues sit on the metro or a short ride apart. Leblon, Copacabana and Catete are all on or near Line 1, which makes hopping between events simple.

Barra da Tijuca, where Roberto Carlos plays, is further out, so allow extra time by car or app. As a result, plan your journey home before a late show lets out.

On money, most tickets sell in reais through Sympla, Fever or venue box offices. Card payments are widely accepted, though a little cash helps at street stalls and smaller bars.

Practical Tips for the Weekend

First, buy concert and theatre tickets only through official platforms such as Sympla and Fever. Because demand is high, resale scams do circulate on social media.

Second, claim any free voucher, like the one for Fiesta Latina, well before you arrive. Otherwise the free window may close by the time you reach the door.

Finally, keep the FX in mind when you budget. At about 5.2 reais to the dollar, a full night out here still costs far less than in most northern cities.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s on in Rio this weekend, 15-16 August 2026?

Highlights include Caio Blat’s play ‘Subversão Kafka’ at Teatro Prio in Leblon, Singles’ Day parties such as Fiesta Latina at Tau in Copacabana. A free Festa Agostina street party at the Museu da República, and Roberto Carlos at Qualistage.

How much do tickets cost?

The Caio Blat play runs R$60 to R$120 (US$12 to US$23). Roberto Carlos starts from about R$210 (US$40).

How do I buy tickets and get in free?

Most tickets sell online through Sympla or Fever, or at venue box offices. For Fiesta Latina at Tau, entry is free before midnight if you claim a Sympla voucher in advance.

What is happening for Singles’ Day in Rio?

Saturday 15 August is the Dia dos Solteiros. Bars across Copacabana, Baixo Gávea and Botafogo run themed parties, with Fiesta Latina ‘Chévere’ at Tau the easiest option for visitors.

Sources: Perplexity sonar-pro fact-check (14 August 2026); O Globo RioShow and G1 Guia RJ weekend agendas; Sympla, Fever and Qualistage listings; Teatro Prio and agendaculturalriodejaneiro.com; Museu da República; Banco Central do Brasil exchange rate.

World.title: What’s On in São Paulo This Weekend: Free Shows, Comedy and Food
World.content:
Brazil · Weekend

Key Facts — When Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August 2026, with a Friday-night warm-up on 14 August.

— Free Ana Cañas, Bixiga 70, Zeca Baleiro and Luedji Luna play free on Avenida São João on Sunday 16 August, part of the city’s Festival do Patrimônio.

— Ticketed Roupa Nova’s ‘Simplesmente’ plays Espaço Unimed on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August; tickets run about R$310 to R$2,000 (US$59 to US$383).

— Comedy and food Stand-up at Bixiga Comedy on Saturday 15 August from R$30 (US$6); a free street-food fair on Avenida São João on Sunday, dishes R$25 to R$45 (US$5 to US$9).

— Exchange rate Prices converted at 1 USD = 5.22 BRL (14 August 2026).

From free open-air concerts on Avenida São João to a bookstore-lined night of stand-up. Here is how to fill Saturday and Sunday without blowing your budget.

Avenida Paulista in São Paulo, home to the Livraria Cultura bookstore. The city’s cultural calendar is packed over the weekend of 15-16 August 2026. Illustrative photo. (Photo: Wilfredor, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.)

If you are looking for things to do in São Paulo this weekend. You are in luck, because Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August 2026 are unusually full.

The city’s month-long heritage festival brings a run of free open-air concerts. There is a two-night arena show, stand-up comedy, a street-food fair and a new blockbuster in cinemas.

We have pulled together the confirmed events, with dates, venues and what you will actually pay. So you can plan before your Saturday fills up.

A packed weekend on almost any budget

The good news is that this is one of those rare weekends where you do not need a big budget to have a great time. Several of the headline events are completely free.

And the paid ones span everything from a R$30 comedy ticket to a proper arena concert. Most of the action is clustered in the Centro and Barra Funda areas, which are easy to reach on the Metrô.

That makes it simple to string a few things together across the two days. Below we run through the free shows first, then the ticketed concerts, comedy.

Food and film, and finish with getting-around tips and what everything costs.

Free concerts on Avenida São João

The single best free plan is on Sunday 16 August. As part of São Paulo’s Festival do Patrimônio.

The city closes a stretch of Avenida São João in the Centro and turns it into an open-air stage. The Palco São João.

The line-up is genuinely strong. Singer Ana Cañas opens at 1:00pm, the Afrobeat band Bixiga 70 follows at 3:00pm.

Zeca Baleiro brings his ‘Baile do Baleiro’ set at 5:00pm, and Luedji Luna closes the night at 7:30pm. Every one of these shows is free, with no ticket needed.

The festival runs from 8 to 16 August across dozens of venues. But Sunday on Avenida São João is the big finale, so arrive early if you want a good spot.

Roupa Nova plays two nights at Espaço Unimed

If you would rather sit down for a classic Brazilian pop night. Roupa Nova bring their intimate ‘Simplesmente’ show to the Espaço Unimed in Barra Funda on both weekend nights.

The Saturday 15 August show starts at 10:00pm, with doors from 8:00pm. There is an extra date on Sunday 16 August in the evening as well, so you have two chances to catch them.

Tickets run from about R$310 in the cheaper sectors up to around R$2,000 for premium seats, roughly US$59 to US$383. The venue sits at Rua Tagipuru 795 and is a short walk from Barra Funda station.

Buy through the official ticket sellers rather than social-media resellers, and check the exact start time on your ticket. As the Sunday show time has been listed slightly differently across platforms.

Stand-up comedy in Bela Vista

For a cheaper night out, there is a stand-up comedy show at Bixiga Comedy on Saturday 15 August at 9:00pm. The venue is in the lively Bixiga district of Bela Vista, at Rua Rui Barbosa 574.

It is a multi-comedian format billed as ‘Pé na Estrada’, so you get several acts in one sitting. The show is recommended for ages 16 and up.

Tickets are a bargain: R$30 (about US$6) for one, or R$50 (about US$10) for a pair, plus the usual booking fee. Portuguese-language humour, so it helps to have a little of the language under your belt.

Street food and a heritage festival

The Festival do Patrimônio is not only about music. On Sunday 16 August, the same Avenida São João hosts an open-air gastronomy fair, ‘Sabores de São Paulo’, from 10:00am to 6:00pm.

Around a dozen restaurants and new ventures from the Centro area set up stalls, each serving an exclusive dish. Plates are priced between R$25 and R$45, roughly US$5 to US$9.

So you can graze your way along the avenue for very little. Entry to the fair is free; you only pay for what you eat.

It pairs neatly with the free concerts on the same street, making Sunday an easy all-day plan in the city centre.

A new Anne Hathaway film in cinemas

If the weather turns, there is a big new release to catch. Anne Hathaway’s latest film, ‘O Fim da Rua’ (original title ‘The End of Oak Street’).

Opened in Brazilian cinemas on Thursday 13 August, so it is showing all weekend. It is an action-adventure with a science-fiction streak, co-starring Ewan McGregor.

And it is playing in standard rooms as well as IMAX around the city. Note that this is a different film from ‘O Diabo Veste Prada 2’.

The long-awaited sequel that already opened in Brazil back in April. Check your neighbourhood cinema for session times and whether it is dubbed or subtitled.

Fafá de Belém kicks off the weekend on Friday

The weekend gets an early start on Friday 14 August. When Amazonian singer Fafá de Belém celebrates 50 years on stage with her ‘Fafá 50’ show at Cine Joia.

The venue is in Liberdade, at Praça Carlos Gomes 82, in the city centre, with doors from 8:00pm. It is a paid event, with tickets advertised from around R$60 to R$160 (about US$11 to US$31) depending on the sector.

Tickets are sold online through the Shotgun platform. Prices have been listed differently across guides, so confirm the current figure before you buy.

Coming up next weekend: SP Gastronomia

If you cannot fit everything in, keep the following weekend free. SP Gastronomia 2026, one of the city’s biggest food festivals.

Runs at Parque Villa-Lobos over two weekends: Friday 21 to Sunday 23 August, and Friday 28 to Sunday 30 August. First-lot tickets start at R$77 full price, or R$38.50 for the half-price ‘meia’ category.

About US$15 and US$7, sold through the official channels. The park is on the west side of the city, at Avenida Professor Fonseca Rodrigues 2001.

And is a pleasant green space to spend an afternoon of tastings.

Getting around São Paulo this weekend

The Metrô is your best friend for the events in São Paulo this weekend. Avenida São João in the Centro is walkable from the República and Anhangabaú stations, both on busy lines.

For Roupa Nova at Espaço Unimed, get off at Barra Funda, which links the Metrô. The CPTM trains and the intercity bus terminal, so it is well connected from most of the city.

Ride-hailing apps work well, but prices climb sharply when a concert lets out. Walking a few blocks away from the venue before you order a car can save you a fair bit on the night.

Practical tips and what you’ll pay

First, carry a little cash. The free street-food stalls and smaller venues often prefer it, even though the arena and official ticket sites take cards.

Second, plan around the free events. Which are the best value: the Sunday concerts and food fair on Avenida São João cost nothing to attend.

Build your paid plans, like Roupa Nova or comedy, around them. Finally, if you are still deciding what to do in São Paulo this weekend.

Aim to reach the free Avenida São João shows well before the headline acts, as the central location draws big crowds. All prices here are converted at 1 US dollar to 5.22 reais, the rate on 14 August 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What free things can I do in São Paulo this weekend?

On Sunday 16 August, Avenida São João in the Centro hosts free open-air concerts by Ana Cañas (1:00pm). Bixiga 70 (3:00pm), Zeca Baleiro (5:00pm) and Luedji Luna (7:30pm), plus a free street-food fair from 10:00am to 6:00pm.

How much are Roupa Nova tickets and where do I buy them?

Roupa Nova play the Espaço Unimed in Barra Funda on Saturday 15 August at 10:00pm and again on Sunday 16 August. Tickets run from about R$310 to R$2,000, roughly US$59 to US$383, and should be bought through the official sellers rather than resellers.

Is there stand-up comedy in São Paulo this weekend?

Yes. Bixiga Comedy in Bela Vista (Rua Rui Barbosa 574) has a multi-act stand-up show.

Which new film is out this weekend?

Anne Hathaway’s ‘O Fim da Rua’ (‘The End of Oak Street’), an action-adventure with Ewan McGregor. Opened in Brazilian cinemas on Thursday 13 August and is showing all weekend, including in IMAX.

Sources: Perplexity sonar-pro fact-check (14 August 2026); São Paulo city culture department (Festival do Patrimônio); Folha de S.Paulo Guia and G1 SP agendas; CNN Brasil (Sabores de São Paulo); Espaço Unimed and official ticketing listings; AdoroCinema and Ingresso.com (O Fim da Rua); exchange rate from dated FX data.

World.title: Léo Santana Lights Up Salvador’s Pagobinho as Samba Fills the Weekend
World.content:
Brazil · Weekend

Key Facts — Pagobinho Sun 16 Aug 2026, 1pm, WET Eventos, Av. Luís Viana Filho 9581, Paralela; special guest Léo Santana. Tickets R$90–R$600 (about US$17–US$115).

— Samba de Caboclo (10th edition) — Sat 15 Aug 2026, 2pm, Clube Fantoches da Euterpe, Rua Democrata 18. Tickets sold online.

— Sambaiana at Casa Rosa Sat 15 Aug 2026, from 9pm, Rio Vermelho. Tickets R$60/R$30 first batch, R$80/R$40 second batch (about US$12–US$15 full).

— Illy Canta Belo Sun 16 Aug 2026, 5pm; a tribute to pagode-romântico star Belo.

— Money note buy tickets online in advance; US$1 was worth about R$5.20 in mid-August 2026.

A newcomer’s guide to Salvador’s samba-soaked weekend, from a beachside pagode party to a tenth-birthday roda in the old town.

Léo Santana (right, with Ivete Sangalo) is a special guest at Salvador’s Pagobinho party on Sunday 16 August 2026. (Photo: Tatiana Azeviche / Turismo Bahia, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons.)

Léo Santana, Salvador’s larger-than-life pagode showman. Headlines a weekend when the Bahian capital seems to breathe samba from Friday night through Sunday evening.

A Weekend Wrapped in Samba

If you have just moved to Salvador, this is a fine weekend to learn why locals call it Brazil’s capital of joy. Because the city’s calendar leans hard into live music.

You can bounce from a beachside pagode party to an intimate samba roda in a colonial courtyard without ever leaving town. This roundup pulls together the verified samba and pagode events happening across Salvador on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August 2026.

With the dates, venues, and ticket prices you actually need. Everything below was checked against the city’s official cultural agenda, so you can plan with confidence instead of guesswork.

Léo Santana Lights Up the Pagobinho Party

The weekend’s biggest draw is Pagobinho, a new pagode party making its debut on Sunday 16 August 2026 at WET Eventos. On Avenida Luís Viana Filho 9581 in the Paralela corridor.

Doors and music start early, at 1pm, so this is an afternoon-into-evening affair rather than a late night. The project is led by singer Fabinho, with sets from the bands Príncipe, Farias, and Caju Pra Baixo.

However, the headline surprise is a special guest appearance by Léo Santana, the towering Bahian star affectionately nicknamed GG. Whose booming voice and stadium energy tend to turn any gathering into a full-blown block party.

Tickets run from R$90 to R$600 (roughly US$17 to US$115), depending on the sector, and they are sold online in advance. Since the cheaper batches for a Léo Santana appearance rarely last, it is worth buying as soon as you decide to go.

What Pagode and Pagobinho Actually Mean

If the words are new to you, here is the friendly version. Samba is the broad rhythm at the root of it all; pagode is its warmer, more relaxed cousin.

Born from backyard gatherings where friends circle around a table, share beer and food, and sing together for hours. Instead of a formal concert, think of a joyful, informal jam that everyone is invited to join.

Pagobinho, then, is simply the affectionate, playful name for this particular pagode party. And the diminutive ‘-inho’ ending signals something cozy and fun rather than grand and stiff.

In short, you do not need to know the words to belong. Once the percussion starts, clapping along and swaying is more than enough.

Samba de Caboclo Marks Ten Editions

For a more traditional roda, head to Samba de Caboclo, which celebrates its tenth edition in Salvador on Saturday 15 August 2026. Originally a Rio de Janeiro project, it has put down deep roots in Bahia, and this milestone show starts at 2pm.

The setting is Clube Fantoches da Euterpe, a historic social club at Rua Democrata 18. Tickets are sold online through the event’s page; because prices were not publicly confirmed at the time of writing.

Check the listing before you go rather than turning up expecting to pay at the door.

Sambaiana Takes Over Casa Rosa

Over in bohemian Rio Vermelho. The band Sambaiana plays Casa Rosa on Saturday 15 August 2026 as part of the venue’s ‘a_gosto da Casa’ series.

Music runs from around 9pm, so this one is the classic Saturday-night option after dinner. The set weaves samba with original songs and a strong female voice on stage.

Making it a lovely introduction to the neighborhood’s live-music scene. Tickets are wallet-friendly: the first batch costs R$60 full price or R$30 half (about US$12 or US$6).

While the second batch rises to R$80 and R$40 (about US$15 or US$8).

One More for Sunday: Illy Sings Belo

If you still have energy on Sunday, Illy Canta Belo lands on 16 August 2026 at 5pm. The show is a tribute to Belo, one of the best-loved names in pagode-romântico, the softer, love-song side of the genre.

It is an easygoing, sing-along kind of afternoon, and a gentle counterpoint to the high-octane Pagobinho happening the same day. Confirm the venue and ticket details on the city agenda before heading out, since those specifics can shift close to showtime.

How to Get Tickets

Almost everything here is sold online, so set yourself up before the weekend. Most Brazilian ticketing platforms accept international cards, though a local CPF number is sometimes requested.

If you have one from your residency paperwork, keep it handy at checkout. Watch for the ‘meia-entrada’ (half-price) option, which applies to students, people over 60.

And a few other groups, provided you can show valid ID at the gate. Otherwise, buy the full-price ‘inteira’ ticket to avoid any hassle on arrival.

Getting There and Getting Around

Salvador is spread out, so plan your transport by neighborhood. The Paralela venue for Pagobinho sits along a major avenue well served by ride apps.

Which are usually the simplest way to arrive and, more importantly, to get home afterward. Rio Vermelho, by contrast, is compact and walkable once you are there, with plenty of bars and restaurants clustered nearby.

Because parking is tight and nights run long, most residents skip driving and rely on Uber or 99 instead.

Where to Eat and Stay Nearby

Rio Vermelho is the tastiest base for a music weekend. Before a show, join the queue at one of the acarajé stands run by the traditionally dressed baianas.

Where a fried black-eyed-pea fritter stuffed with shrimp and vatapá makes the perfect pre-gig bite for just a few reais. For visitors, this neighborhood also offers the widest choice of guesthouses and small hotels, so you can walk home after Sambaiana.

If you are near Paralela for Pagobinho, the modern hotels along the avenue and toward the airport are a practical, comfortable option.

Tips for a Smooth Night Out

A few small habits go a long way. Carry a little cash for street food and tips even though most venues take cards.

And keep your phone tucked away in crowds, as you would in any big city. Meanwhile, dress light: Salvador stays warm and humid year-round, and you will be moving.

Finally, pace yourself across the weekend. With a Léo Santana afternoon, a tenth-anniversary roda, and a Rio Vermelho night all within reach.

The smart move is to pick two, arrive early, and let the samba carry the rest.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where does Léo Santana perform in Salvador this weekend?

Léo Santana appears as a special guest at the Pagobinho party on Sunday 16 August 2026. Starting at 1pm, at WET Eventos on Avenida Luís Viana Filho 9581 in Paralela.

How much do tickets cost?

Pagobinho tickets run from R$90 to R$600 (about US$17 to US$115). Sambaiana at Casa Rosa costs R$60/R$30 in the first batch and R$80/R$40 in the second (about US$12 to US$15 full price).

How do I buy tickets?

Buy online in advance through the venues’ ticketing pages. Look for the half-price ‘meia-entrada’ option if you qualify, and bring valid ID to claim it at the door.

What is pagode, exactly?

Pagode is a warm, informal offshoot of samba, born from backyard gatherings of friends singing together. You do not need to know the songs to join in; clapping and swaying along is enough.

World.title: Viva Perifa Brings a Giant Street Mural to a Salvador Public School
World.content:
Brazil · Culture

Key Facts — What Viva Perifa nas Comunidades, running its first Salvador edition through public-school murals and graffiti workshops

— Where Escola Municipal Novo Horizonte, in the Sussuarana neighborhood of Salvador, Bahia

— When Activities run from August to November 2026

— Highlight A 178 m² mural on the school’s outer wall by graffiti artist Marcos ‘Cabuloso’ Costa, plus an indoor mural made with students by Niiny Santos

— Cost A publicly funded community project; the outdoor mural sits on a street-facing wall, free for anyone to walk past and see

A first-of-its-kind community art project is turning a Sussuarana schoolyard into grassroots Bahian street art. With a 178-square-metre mural rising on a public wall.

Illustrative photo: colorful graffiti street art on an urban wall in Recife, Brazil. Viva Perifa is painting a 178 m2 mural on a Salvador public school in Sussuarana between August and November 2026. (Photo: Leonaardog, CC0, Wikimedia Commons.)

Viva Perifa has arrived in Salvador for the first time. And it is doing something quietly wonderful: turning the walls of a neighborhood public school into grassroots Bahian street art.

For expats who love the color and grit of Brazil’s mural scene. This is a fresh reason to look beyond the tourist postcard of Pelourinho.

Viva Perifa Comes to Salvador for the First Time

This is the debut Salvador edition of Viva Perifa nas Comunidades, a project that brings graffiti. Murals, and art workshops into public schools in peripheral neighborhoods.

Because it is the first time the initiative has landed in the Bahian capital. There is a real sense of occasion around it.

The action is unfolding at Escola Municipal Novo Horizonte, in the Sussuarana neighborhood, between August and November 2026. In short.

A working schoolyard on the edge of the city is being reimagined as a canvas for local artists and the children who study there.

What the Project Is Really About

At heart, this is community art rather than a museum show. The project revitalizes school spaces through urban art and hands-on cultural workshops.

Using graffiti as a tool for education, pride, and neighborhood identity. It has previously worked in schools elsewhere in Brazil, including flood-affected communities in Rio Grande do Sul, before reaching Salvador.

So if you come expecting ticket booths and gallery lighting, adjust your expectations. The value here is watching a peripheral neighborhood turn its own walls into an open-air gallery.

Made by and for the people who live around them.

The School and the Sussuarana Neighborhood

Everything centers on Escola Municipal Novo Horizonte, a municipal school in Sussuarana, a large working-class district inland from Salvador’s coastal tourist strip. Sussuarana is not on the standard visitor circuit, which is exactly the point: the art is meant to serve the community first.

For newcomers to Bahia, it helps to think of the project as part of the everyday fabric of a residential neighborhood. The murals are not staged for outsiders, yet the biggest one will be plainly visible to anyone passing on the street.

A 178-Square-Metre Mural on a Public Wall

The centerpiece is a 178-square-metre mural on the school’s outer wall, created by graffiti artist Marcos Costa, better known as Cabuloso. Because it faces the street, this is the piece most people will actually encounter, no appointment required.

That scale is significant for a neighborhood school. A mural of that size becomes a landmark.

A splash of color and storytelling that reshapes how a stretch of Sussuarana looks and feels for years to come.

Workshops and a Mural Made by the Students

Inside the school, the project runs graffiti and visual-arts workshops for about 60 students aged 10 to 12, split into two groups. They learn the history of graffiti, meet Salvador’s own urban artists, and pick up drawing and painting techniques.

The workshops are led by visual artist, muralist, and graffiti artist Niiny Santos. At the end, Niiny works with the students to produce an indoor mural.

So the children are not just spectators but co-authors of the art on their own school walls.

The Themes: Diversity, Sustainability, Inclusion

The subject of the big external mural is chosen together with the school community, guided by three themes: diversity, sustainability, and inclusion. As a result, the finished wall reflects local voices rather than an outside artist’s fixed idea.

For a resident trying to understand Bahian culture, that participatory process is half the story. The mural becomes a snapshot of what this particular community wants to say about itself in 2026.

Who Is Behind Viva Perifa in Salvador

The Salvador edition is produced by Yabá Consultoria and co-produced by Aflora Cultural. Funding comes through Brazil’s Lei Federal de Incentivo à Cultura, the country’s federal cultural-incentive law, with corporate sponsorship from Leroy Merlin.

That backing matters because it is what keeps the workshops free for the children and puts a professional-scale mural on a public-school wall. In other words.

A mix of public policy and private sponsorship is paying for grassroots art in a neighborhood that rarely gets it.

How to See the Art Respectfully

Let’s be honest about access. The organizers have not published visitor hours, a street address for drop-ins, or a formal exhibition format.

Because this is a working school and a community program, not a gallery. The workshops and indoor mural are for the enrolled students, not the general public.

What you can freely enjoy is the large outdoor mural. Which lives on a street-facing wall in Sussuarana as it takes shape between August and November.

If you go, treat it as you would any residential neighborhood: be low-key. Do not disrupt the school day, and let the work speak for itself.

Why It Matters for Salvador’s Street-Art Scene

Salvador’s creative energy is famous, but most visitors only ever see it in the historic center. Projects like this one push that energy outward, into the neighborhoods where most Bahians actually live.

And that is where a lot of the freshest work is happening. For expats and long-stay residents who want to understand the city beyond the postcard.

Keeping an eye on grassroots initiatives is the move. This mural is one small, colorful marker of a much bigger community art movement taking root across the periphery.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Viva Perifa happening in Salvador?

The activities run between August and November 2026 at Escola Municipal Novo Horizonte in Sussuarana. The large outdoor mural takes shape across that period.

Where exactly is it, and can I visit?

It is at Escola Municipal Novo Horizonte in the Sussuarana neighborhood of Salvador, Bahia. The 178-square-metre mural is on the school’s outer, street-facing wall, so you can see it from the street.

How much does it cost?

There is no admission and no ticket. It is a publicly funded community project, so the outdoor mural is simply free to walk past and enjoy from the street.

Who is making the murals?

Graffiti artist Marcos ‘Cabuloso’ Costa is painting the 178-square-metre external mural. While artist Niiny Santos leads the student workshops and the indoor mural made with the children.

Sources: Sources: Alô Alô Bahia (13 August 2026); Viva Perifa project communications. Fact-checked August 2026.

World.title: This Week in Bogotá: Concerts, Free Festivals and Earthquake Benefits
World.content:
Colombia · Weekend

Key Facts — When Friday 14 to Wednesday 19 August 2026, with a long weekend: Monday 17 August is a public holiday (Assumption of Mary, moved under Ley Emiliani).

— Benefit concerts ‘Resonancias’ (Fri 14 Aug, 7:00pm) and the Bogotá Philharmonic solidarity concert (Sat 15 Aug, 4:00pm) at Auditorio Fabio Lozano; tickets COP 25,000-35,000 (US$8-11), proceeds to earthquake victims.

— Big show Morat’s Ya Es Mañana tour at Movistar Arena on Fri 14, Sat 15 and Sun 16 August, 9:00pm; tickets COP 195,000-730,000 (US$62-233) via TuBoleta.

— Free Festival de Verano runs city-wide all month; the weekend brings Diverparques family days, canoeing at Simón Bolívar and a skating record on Ciclovía, all free.

— Exchange rate Prices converted at 1 USD = 3,127.51 COP (TRM, 14 August 2026).

A long holiday weekend, two earthquake benefit concerts, Morat at the arena. And a city-wide free festival: here is how to fill your days from Friday to Wednesday.

A panorama over Bogotá, Colombia. The city’s cultural calendar is packed during the August summer festival and the holiday weekend. Illustrative photo. (Photo: Martin St-Amant (S23678), CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.)

If you are living in or passing through Bogotá this week, the timing is lucky. A long holiday weekend, a stacked cultural calendar and several benefit events for earthquake victims all land between Friday and Wednesday.

Whether you have a big budget or none at all, there is plenty on. We have pulled together the confirmed events, with dates, venues and what you will pay.

So you can plan before the weekend fills up.

A long weekend to build your plans around

First, the good news for your calendar. Monday 17 August 2026 is a public holiday in Colombia, marking the Assumption of Mary.

The feast falls on Saturday 15 August, but under the Ley Emiliani it moves to the following Monday. As a result, you get a three-day weekend from Saturday to Monday.

That matters for planning. Many workplaces close on the Monday, so museums, parks and venues tend to be busier than usual.

Benefit concerts for earthquake victims

The strongest reason to go out this week is also the most meaningful. After the 10 August earthquake, Bogotá’s music world has organised two solidarity concerts.

First up is ‘Resonancias’ on Friday 14 August at 7:00pm. It brings together Antonio Arnedo, El Colectivo Colombia and the Bogotá Women’s Philharmonic under conductor Natalí Espinosa.

The venue is the Auditorio Fabio Lozano at the Jorge Tadeo Lozano University, downtown. Because every peso of ticket revenue goes to earthquake victims, it is an easy night to feel good about.

Then on Saturday 15 August at 4:00pm, the Orquesta Filarmónica de Bogotá plays a solidarity concert at the same venue. Conductor Enluis Montes Olivar leads, with pianist Daniel Díaz-Padilla as soloist.

Tickets for both run COP 25,000 to 35,000 (about US$8 to US$11). In addition, the auditorium doubles as a drop-off point for donated supplies, so bring what you can spare.

Morat at Movistar Arena — and a fundraiser too

The big-ticket event this week is Colombian pop band Morat, who bring their Ya Es Mañana world tour home. They play Movistar Arena on Friday 14, Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August, each night at 9:00pm.

Tickets range from COP 195,000 in the upper tiers to COP 730,000 for the fan tribune, roughly US$62 to US$233. They are sold through TuBoleta, the official operator, so avoid resellers.

There is a charitable angle here as well. The band is setting up donation points at the arena and channelling part of the proceeds toward rebuilding schools through UNICEF.

Free festivals across the city

If money is tight, the Festival de Verano de Bogotá has you covered. Now in its 29th edition, it runs from 31 July to 31 August with more than 60 mostly free events.

This weekend the family-friendly Diverparques days spread across neighbourhood parks on Saturday 15 and Sunday 16 August. From 9:00am, with games and activities at no cost.

Sports fans have options too. A national canoeing Grand Prix takes over the lake at Parque Simón Bolívar on Saturday 15 August from 7:00am.

While an archery championship runs both days at Parque El Country in Usaquén. For something quirkier.

A mass skating attempt at a human-train record rolls along the Avenida Calle 26 Ciclovía on Sunday 16 August from 8:00am. All of it is free to watch.

Theatre and open-air shows

Bogotá’s stages stay busy this week as well. At the open-air La Media Torta, a free narrated retelling of Homer’s Iliad plays on Saturday 15 August at noon.

Part of the city’s theatre and circus festival. Over at the Teatro Colón, the popular Candlelight series continues on Friday 14 August.

With tribute programmes to ABBA and to classic rock across the evening. The Teatro Mayor Julio Mario Santo Domingo also has dance in its studio space on Friday 14 and Saturday 15 August.

Check each venue’s site for the latest ticket details before you go.

Museums and gardens on the cheap

A long weekend is perfect for the city’s museums, and several are a bargain. The Gold Museum, one of Bogotá’s must-sees, is free for everyone on Sundays, including Sunday 16 August.

On other days it costs COP 10,000 for nationals and COP 21,000 for foreign visitors, roughly US$3 to US$7. Children under 12 and adults over 62 always enter free.

The Museo Nacional opens its rooms free every Wednesday from 2:00pm to 5:00pm, so Wednesday 19 August is your window. The MamBo modern-art museum charges COP 18,000 to 25,000 (about US$6 to US$8).

A green break in the Bogotá agenda

For fresh air, the José Celestino Mutis Botanical Garden is a calm counterpoint to the festival crowds. Since late July, one general ticket also covers the Tropicario greenhouse.

Admission is COP 16,000 for Colombian nationals and COP 38,000 for foreign visitors, about US$5 and US$12. Children under 5 and adults over 60 go in free.

It is an easy morning out before the afternoon events start. Meanwhile, the garden’s shaded paths are a good place to escape the holiday-weekend bustle.

Getting around during a busy week

Public transport is your friend across this stretch. Movistar Arena sits near the El Campín stadium in Teusaquillo and is well served by TransMilenio and buses.

For the free festival events, Parque Simón Bolívar and the Ciclovía are central and walkable, though weekend crowds are heavy. As a result, allow extra time getting home after a big show.

Ride-hailing apps and taxis work well, but prices climb when concerts let out. So walking a few blocks before ordering a car can save you money on the night.

Practical tips for the weekend

First, carry a little cash. Many free festival stalls and small venues prefer pesos, even though cards work at the big arenas and ticket sites.

Second, buy concert tickets only through official channels such as TuBoleta. Because demand is high this week, resale scams are common.

Finally, remember the Monday holiday. Some offices and banks close, so run any errands on Friday and keep the long weekend free for the fun.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the earthquake benefit events in Bogotá this week?

Two solidarity concerts at the Auditorio Fabio Lozano: ‘Resonancias’ on Friday 14 August at 7:00pm. And the Bogotá Philharmonic on Saturday 15 August at 4:00pm.

How much do Morat tickets cost and where do I buy them?

Morat plays Movistar Arena on 14, 15 and 16 August at 9:00pm. Tickets range from COP 195,000 to COP 730,000, roughly US$62 to US$233, and are sold through the official operator TuBoleta.

What free things can I do in Bogotá this week?

The Festival de Verano offers dozens of free events. Including Diverparques family days and a canoeing Grand Prix at Parque Simón Bolívar on 15-16 August.

Is Monday 17 August a holiday in Colombia?

Yes. Monday 17 August 2026 is a public holiday for the Assumption of Mary, moved from Saturday 15 August under the Ley Emiliani.

Sources: Perplexity sonar-pro fact-check (14 August 2026); IDRD Festival de Verano de Bogotá agenda; Movistar Arena and TuBoleta listings; Teatro Colón and La Media Torta calendars; Banco de la República TRM; Museo del Oro and Jardín Botánico de Bogotá tariffs.

World.title: What’s On in Puebla This Weekend: DJ Snake and a Free Book Fair
World.content:
Mexico · Weekend

Key Facts — DJ Snake, free Saturday 15 August 2026, Festival Frecuencias at Plaza de la Victoria; the French star’s set is billed for around 16:00 and entry is free, no ticket needed.

— Book fair, free The Feria Internacional del Libro Puebla (FILIP) runs 14–23 August, so it is open all weekend across the Zocalo, Teatro de la Ciudad and Capilla del Arte UDLAP, with 300-plus free activities.

— FILIP highlights Saturday 15 brings the staged ‘Requiem por Juana Ines de la Cruz’ at the Teatro de la Ciudad at 16:00; Sunday 16 offers ‘Don Quijote de la Mancha’ with Omar Ruiz at 18:00.

— Looking ahead, ticketed Tecate Comuna 2026 (Foro Cholula, Saturday 28 November) opens its Banamex presale Tuesday 18 August and general sale Wednesday 19 August via eTicket, from MXN 1,590 (about US$93).

— Money Everything on this weekend’s main bill is free; the exchange guide used here is roughly 17.1 pesos to the US dollar, mid-August 2026.

From a free superstar DJ set on the Plaza de la Victoria to a ten-day book fair filling the historic center. Here is how to make the most of two busy days.

The cathedral of Puebla de Zaragoza at dawn, at the heart of the Centro Historico where the FILIP book fair runs all weekend. (Photo: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.)
