World.title: Antonio Maíllo: “Marruecos ha cometido una acción criminal con muertes. Hay que replantearse todo”
World.content:
El coordinador federal de Izquierda Unida defiende en EL PAÍS un cambio total en las relaciones diplomáticas con el país vecino tras la entrada masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta

Antonio Maíllo (Lucena, Córdoba, 59 años) está estos días en la sierra de Huelva, donde sigue pendiente de los incendios que asolan a la provincia con más de 25.000 hectáreas calcinadas. El coordinador general de Izquierda Unida atiende a EL PAÍS por teléfono y defiende un cambio radical en las relaciones diplomáticas con Marruecos, a quien tacha de cometer una “acción criminal” que ha provocado muertes en Ceuta.

Pregunta. ¿Se sabe realmente qué ha pasado en Ceuta?

Respuesta. Queremos saberlo. La obligación del Gobierno es explicar todo con absoluta transparencia porque la sociedad española y ceutí lo merece. Ante un estado como el de Marruecos, que desprecia la vida de sus ciudadanos, España tiene que marcar la diferencia. Hay que explicar todo sin ningún tipo de prejuicio o falso tacticismo para no molestar al vecino.

P. Parece cabreado. ¿Le quedan aún muchas respuestas?

R. La propia declaración de Pedro Sánchez diciendo que había una violación de la integridad territorial. Si uno declara esa situación, no puede no convocar al Consejo Nacional de Seguridad o establecer un gabinete de crisis. Y, en segundo lugar, si se ha producido una violación, es porque alguien la ha ejecutado. Evidentemente, ha sido Marruecos. Hemos hecho una petición de reunión de la comisión de secretos oficiales en el Congreso por si determinada información solo puede darse allí y ver también si hay algún informe del CNI alertando de ese ataque híbrido unos días antes.

P. El ministro de Exteriores dijo este martes que hasta la última persona que entró irregularmente en Ceuta volverá a Marruecos.

R. Me sorprende que el ministro tenga esa seguridad. Es muy complicado lo que dice porque también está el derecho al asilo. A todas las personas les existe un procedimiento que tiene que ser respetado y el Gobierno de España tiene que garantizarlo. Creo que hay una urgencia de carácter humanitario en estos momentos, en los que, por ejemplo, creo que hay que atender como prioridad a los solicitantes de asilo y de acogida humanitaria para que vengan a los centros de la península que no están saturados. Y, por otro lado, la atención de los menores que hay en Ceuta.

P. ¿Cree que Marruecos ha utilizado la presión migratoria como herramienta política?

R. En Marruecos no se mueve una hoja sin el propio Gobierno. Que 72.000 personas [80.000, según las etimaciones que maneja el Ejecutivo] fueran como una ola de camino a Ceuta y que Marruecos lo dejara hacer es una acción absolutamente irresponsable y criminal. El Estado de Marruecos ha cometido una acción criminal que ha provocado la muerte de personas. Es una irresponsabilidad absoluta de un gobierno y un Estado con el que hay que replantearse todas las relaciones.

Antonio Maíllo, durante la entrevista el día 11 de agosto. PACO PUENTES

P. ¿En qué consistiría ese giro estratégico?

R. Aquí nos hemos sentido solos. Primero, la Unión Europea tiene que tener una posición común. Segundo, creemos que los intereses estratégicos de buena vecindad con Marruecos no pueden descartar la posición histórica de España con respecto al Sáhara y la necesidad de un referéndum de autodeterminación bajo el amparo de la ONU. Y tercero, una ley sin la cual no puede haber relaciones de buena vecindad. Hay que establecer una relación de lealtad entre los organismos de información de ambos países. O el CNI ha fallado. O las relaciones modélicas que se presumen no han sido tal.

P. Estos días también hemos visto cómo las familias ceutíes están acogiendo a niñas menores de edad porque los centros están saturados. ¿Cómo puede pasar esto en España?

R. Hay una urgencia que es un procedimiento que tiene que tener toda la garantía. Hay que agradecer la atención solidaria de familias que acogen a menores que de lo contrario podían estar en una situación de absoluta fragilidad y vulnerabilidad. Se están haciendo todos los esfuerzos posibles para que el procedimiento sea rápido.

P. Pero el Gobierno actual lleva ya casi siete años en el poder. Da la sensación de que hay una falta de recursos.

R. No es una cuestión de recursos. Se han aumentado los recursos y hay una situación absolutamente insoportable. Por eso, este jueves se ha convocado la comisión sectorial de infancia, donde se va a proceder al reparto que establece la norma y en el que ningún gobierno autonómico se puede negar, porque sería un incumplimiento de la ley.

P. Usted, por cierto, también es partidario de excluir a Marruecos de la organización del Mundial 2030 junto a España y Portugal.

R. Absolutamente. Hay que dar un golpe en la mesa de la FIFA. Y una señal en España de que, evidentemente, Marruecos no está a la altura de una garantía en el trato de los derechos humanos para coorganizar un mundial como el que se quiere hacer solidariamente con Portugal y con España.

P. De hecho, han presentado una Proposición No de Ley en el Congreso, que comparten con Vox. Vox se inclina por votar su propuesta. ¿Y ustedes?

R. Nos opondremos. Vox no tiene ninguna autoridad moral ni política para hacer oportunismo con este asunto, como el Partido Popular. Ninguno de los dos ha dudado en intentar erosionar a nuestro país con sus aliados europeos, como Italia.

P. Pero la finalidad es la misma. Que Marruecos no organice el Mundial con España.

R. Es oportunismo y no es solo oportunismo, sino que está dentro de un marco de deslealtad hacia nuestro país y de no dudar en intentar desestabilizar sin poner el foco en quién ha sido el responsable de esta crisis principal, que es el gobierno de Marruecos.

P. ¿Se ha equivocado el Gobierno con su cambio de posición respecto al Sáhara?

R. El PSOE se ha equivocado siempre con el Sáhara, como se ha equivocado siempre en su relación, cada vez más aislada, con Marruecos. Creo que debería escucharnos con respecto al replanteamiento estratégico que defendemos. Se ha demostrado fracasada la posición y el giro que dio, que fue una traición al pueblo saharaui por Pedro Sánchez, no nos ha servido para nada.

P. Sobre el futuro de la izquierda, la ministra Sira Rego dijo en EL PAÍS el pasado jueves que la izquierda tendría que replantearse ya. ¿Cómo la ve de cara a las próximas generales del año que viene?

R. Hay que presentar un proyecto de país y estamos en condiciones de hacerlo. Yo soy de los que piensan que va a haber elecciones generales antes que las municipales de mayo. Mi previsión es que sean en torno a marzo y el sentido común nos exige construir este proceso, dándonos ya en septiembre y octubre el cumplimiento del proyecto, la presentación de su nombre y las personas que vayan a encabezarlo. Y creo que en esos ritmos todo el mundo está de acuerdo en que tienen que darse en el próximo mes o los dos primeros meses.

P. ¿Han hablado ya con esa figura que va a encabezar el proyecto?

R. El calendario tiene que tener en cuenta, en primer lugar, qué es lo que justifica que nos presentemos, y creo que ya lo hemos hecho, y además hay un punto de representación que puede haber de entre el 11% y el 18% de la población española que se identifica con nuestro proyecto y, por tanto, en esta recolección del proyecto entendemos que es lo más importante, y después, evidentemente, darle forma simbólica a la persona que lo lidere sobre lo que estamos trabajando, evidentemente.

P. Y ya ha habido acercamientos con esa persona...

R. Evidentemente.

World.title: De la ingeniería aeroespacial al quirófano: el primer metamaterial óseo implantado salva la pierna de Pierre
World.content:
El Hospital Gregorio Marañón y la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid desarrollan una tibia con tecnología 3D que le ha permitido a un hombre de 38 años conservar su pierna y poder caminar

Hace unos años, a Pierre, un joven francés de 38 años, le diagnosticaron cáncer. Tras una radiografía y una biopsia, los médicos identificaron que se trataba de un sarcoma óseo de alto grado en la tibia, un tumor agresivo que había crecido rápidamente. Pierre fue tratado en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón, centro de referencia nacional para los sarcomas del aparato locomotor. Los cirujanos consiguieron extirpar el tumor y que conservara la pierna y la articulación, pero esto era solo el primer paso. Tenían que reconstruir parte del hueso para que aquella extremidad pudiera volver a soportar el peso de su cuerpo. La solución llegó de una alianza entre el hospital y la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. Le fabricaron una prótesis ósea de metamaterial personalizada, la primera de estas características en el mundo que se ha implantado en un paciente.

“He vuelto a apoyar la pierna después de dos años y por fin voy a poder caminar de nuevo sin muletas”, cuenta Pierre. La prótesis no la ve ni la siente: “Es lo que tengo y ha salido bien”.

Pierre, durante la rehabilitación, en imágenes cedidas por el Gregorio Marañón.

La pieza dentro de su pierna fue calculada a partir de su propio hueso y fabricada mediante impresión 3D en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón. Su estructura interna, hecha de titanio, está formada por una red de pequeñas barras cuya geometría ha sido calculada para que el implante soporte las cargas de una forma parecida a como lo haría un hueso sano.

La prótesis, que el hospital madrileño ha presentado este viernes, es el resultado de años de colaboración entre ambos centros. Llevan más de una década en el desarrollo de una estructura que permite que médicos, ingenieros, investigadores y otros profesionales participen en el diseño y fabricación de este tipo de soluciones.

Pierre, el paciente recuperado, en imágenes cedidas por el Gregorio Marañón.

Rubén Pérez-Mañanes, subdirector científico del Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria del Gregorio Marañón, asegura que el hospital ha sido pionero en la aplicación de esta tecnología a la medicina. “Este hospital fue el primero en implementar una unidad de este tipo. Cuando las impresoras 3D se utilizaban para hacer maquetas y juguetes, aquí se utilizaban para hacer modelos y réplicas anatómicas de pacientes”, cuenta el también coordinador de la Unidad de Planificación Avanzada y Manufactura 3D (UPAM3D).

Un implante para un paciente único

No existía una solución comercial que respondiera a las necesidades del caso de Pierre. La prótesis había que crearla específicamente para él. “Funcionan por tallas y es el cirujano el que tiene que adaptarlas al paciente. Y aquí lo hacemos a la inversa”, explica Pérez-Mañanes. “Se ha diseñado solo para él. Situamos al paciente en el centro y desarrollamos una cultura de medicina personalizada”, sostiene el médico.

El Instituto de Investigación Sanitaria del hospital mantiene convenios con distintas universidades, entre ellas la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. De ese vínculo surgió el contacto con el equipo de Luis Saucedo-Mora, investigador de la Escuela Técnica Superior de Ingeniería Aeronáutica y del Espacio. Este grupo llevaba años desentrañando estructuras cuya geometría interna permite modificar las propiedades mecánicas de un material.

El cirujano Rubén Pérez-Mañanes, izquierda, y el ingeniero Luis Saucedo-Mora, de la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. Andrea Comas

Tras todo ese trabajo, de investigación y experimentación, lograron aumentar la resistencia del implante con la misma rigidez y distribución que tenía el hueso sano. “Hemos conseguido una metodología con la que podemos ir adaptando la forma para tener la misma función mecánica de antes”, detalla Saucedo-Mora.

Así convirtieron el titanio en una solución a medida

De partida, el material era el titanio, un elemento más pesado que el hueso. Los investigadores tuvieron que aligerar su estructura. Construyeron el interior de la pieza con pequeñas barras de escala milimétrica. “Es una réplica matemática del hueso”, apunta el también profesor de Mecánica del Continuo y Teoría de Estructuras en la Escuela de Ingeniería Aeroespacial de la UPM.

Crearon un gemelo digital de su pierna con imágenes radiológicas. Simularon las cargas que soportaría la tibia al caminar, subir escaleras o sufrir un tropiezo. Con esos datos calcularon la arquitectura interna del implante y orientaron los tornillos hacia las zonas de hueso mejor conservada.

“La prótesis pesa unos 300 gramos, frente a cerca de un kilo de una convencional. Prácticamente, lo mismo que un reloj”, subraya Saucedo-Mora. Además, soporta más de 500 kilos.

Para José María Lamo de Espinosa, director del Departamento de Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología del Hospital Ascires de Valencia, hay dos características principales que diferencian estas prótesis de las tradicionales. La primera es la adaptación a las propiedades mecánicas de cada hueso. “En la cirugía oncológica, muchas veces el tumor marca una resección que no es la estándar para una prótesis convencional”, apunta Lamo de Espinosa, que también es presidente de la Sociedad Española de Investigación en Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología, que ha valorado la presentación del caso de Pierre.

La segunda está en el interior del objeto. “El material está diseñado de tal forma que sea lo más parecido al hueso. No es lo mismo un hueso de un chaval de 20 años que el de una señora de 60”, explica el también miembro de la Sociedad Europea de Oncología Musculoesquelética (Emsos) e investigador en ADAPT BONE, un proyecto europeo y nacional que desarrolla este tipo de tecnología para aplicaciones médicas, entre ellas la oncológica.

Aunque existen muchos proyectos que van en ese sentido, lo que el Hospital Gregorio Marañón y la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid han desarrollado es el primero que ha sido implantado y muestra signos de éxito.

Casi un año después de la intervención, Pierre conserva la pierna y la movilidad de la rodilla. Ha tenido que pasar por una larga rehabilitación y continúa en seguimiento oncológico, pero ha empezado a caminar sin muletas. En este tiempo, sufrió una caída durante la recuperación. La pierna contraria se fracturó, pero el implante de la tibia reconstruida resistió y se mantuvo intacto.

“El coste habitual de un implante como este es de entre 30.000 y 50.000 euros. Este costó 3.000, que es el precio de la impresión 3D”, detalla Pérez-Mañanes. “Pero lo más importante no es el ahorro económico, sino el poder aprovechar recursos para democratizar el acceso a la medicina personalizada”, agrega el médico del Hospital Gregorio Marañón.

De acuerdo con él, pese a toda la tecnología que rodea la prótesis, el objetivo es “humanizar el trabajo”. “Trabajar en equipo. Sin eso no hay medicina, ni salud”. Además, comenta que ya han operado a otros pacientes bajo este método: “Queremos hacer un protocolo, un programa estándar para poder llegar a un mayor volumen de pacientes”.

World.title: Finlay Tarling, ciclista galés de 19 años, muere atropellado durante la Vuelta a Portugal
World.content:
Llora Portugal y el ciclismo, también Gales y el equipo NSN, rotos porque este viernes perdió la vida en la octava etapa de la Vuelta a Portugal el ciclista Finlay Tarling, de 19 años y galés, que formaba en el NSN Development Team, el equipo de desarrollo. Era también el hermano menor de Josh, corredor en el Ineos con gran caché en las cronos, campeón de contrarreloj europeo, así como tercero en el mundo, dos veces campeón británico y ya ganador de una etapa en el Giro de Italia. Y era, claro, hijo de Michael y Dawn, amantes de las dos ruedas. Pero una maldita furgoneta, que circulaba en sentido contrario, lo atropelló. La muerte fue declarada alrededor de las 15.40, a pesar de la rápida intervención de los servicios médicos, que no pudieron revertir el paro cardiorrespiratorio.

La organización, prudente, no se posicionaba sobre lo ocurrido hasta saberlo todo; cómo sucedió, por qué, quién… ya con el caso bajo investigación y el cuerpo de la víctima en el Instituto de Medicina Legal de Viana do Castelo. “Todo lo que sabemos por ahora está en el comunicado conjunto de la Federación Portuguesa de Ciclismo y de la Volta a Portugal. No tenemos información adicional que podamos confirmar en este momento”, resolvían desde dentro ante la persistencia de los periodistas. Pero no salían de la versión de que “había sucedido un gran accidente”, sin más detalle. Pero no hubo que esperar a tanto y fue Tiago Machado, de la Guarda Nacional Republicana (GNR), quien lo corroboró ante los micros de la radio portugués RTP, que sigue a la Volta. Una que, ya confirmó el presidente de la federación ciclista lusa, Cándido Barbosa, continuará hasta su conclusión -no así en la fatídica etapa, que se cortó cuando se supo la magnitud de la tragedia-. Su equipo, a falta de confirmación oficial, no seguirá en la carretera.

“Fin era un miembro muy querido de nuestro equipo, pero lo más importante, era un hijo, un hermano y un amigo para muchos. Se le echará mucho de menos”, expresó el equipo desde la red social X. Y agregó: “Nuestras condolencias están con sus padres, Michael y Dawn, su hermano Josh, y todos los que tuvieron la suerte de llamarle amigo. Descanse en paz”. El presidente de Portugal, António José Seguro, también lamentó lo ocurrido y, en un comunicado, expresó su “profundo pesar por el trágico fallecimiento” del ciclista galés. Días de pena y luto, de lágrimas en la carretera, y en el NSN Development Team, donde también corría esta Volta el español Álvaro García, además del director deportivo Rubén Plaza. La formación continental es el filial del NSN Cycling Team, el proyecto hispano-suizo impulsado por NSN, empresa cofundada por Andrés Iniesta, y Stoneweg.

Pedaleaba estos días con una sonrisa en la cara Tarling, que disputaba su carrera más importante hasta el momento, superando el Tour de Ruanda de este curso, donde selló dos etapas con el segundo y cuarto puesto, además de firmar el bronce en el campeonato junior de contrarreloj. En la Volta, genes Tarling, también brilló en las cronos, undécimo en el prólogo y 15º en la contrarreloj de Águeda. Pero una furgoneta se lo arrebató todo. Una tragedia que se suma a la de 1958, cuando los españoles Raúl Motos y Joaquín Polo fallecieron por deshidratación e insolación, etapa bajo el sol abrasador. Y también sucedió otra terrible desdicha en 1996, porque el coche de dos periodistas -uno era José Santiago, exciclista que venció tres etapas de la Volta- fue embestido por un taxista que se durmió al volante. Finlay Tarling les acompaña ahora en el cielo.

World.title: Fundadora de una empresa de porno para mujeres y contacto de Epstein: sale a la luz la historia de la misteriosa mujer de Dario Amodei
World.content:
Michelle Capocetalo y Cami Clark (a la derecha), cofundadoras de la empresa de porno para mujeres Eddice, en una conferencia en 2010. Clark es hoy la mujer de Dario Amodei, presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic.

El cofundador de Anthropic mantiene tan discreta su vida privada que no se sabía que estaba casado. Su esposa, Cami Clark, tiene una historia tan desconocida que no conoce ni Claude

“Perdona, ¿quién eres?”, escribió el inversor y pedófilo Jeffrey Epstein en un email a Cami Clark en 2012. Cuatro años antes, Epstein se había declarado culpable de prostitución de menores. Clark pretendía que Epstein invirtiera en su empresa de “porno de lujo”, que aspiraba a un público femenino en una industria pensada para los hombres y que tenía como lema “intelectualmente promiscuas”.

Camilla Clark es también la esposa desde 2022 de Dario Amodei, presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic, cuya salida a Bolsa este otoño puede convertir a la pareja en una de las más ricas de Silicon Valley. Este viernes, dos medios estadounidenses, el Wall Street Journal y The Information, han publicado a la vez dos largos perfiles de Clark.

El estado civil de Amodei era un misterio público hasta hace unos meses y el rastro digital de Clark en internet es casi cero. Claude, el célebre chatbot de Anthropic, tampoco sabía que Amodei estaba casado y mucho menos quién era Clark: “Acabas de comprobar en directo que Claude no sabía nada de ella”, responde el modelo sobre la pareja. Según el Journal, “se han hecho esfuerzos para suprimir referencias a ella que había en internet”.

Clark, nacida en 1979 en Reno (Nevada) y cuatro años mayor que Amodei, ha tenido un tortuoso camino hasta la actual cima de la IA. Se casó a los 20 años con un arquitecto de 64, de quien se divorció tres años después. Nunca se licenció en la universidad, se mudó a San Francisco en 1999 y desde entonces trata de escalar social y empresarialmente en uno de los rincones más privilegiados del mundo. Incluso tuvo que declararse en bancarrota en una ocasión. Tras su fracaso con el porno de lujo, intentó montar una app de “dieta social” que convirtió en una empresa de salud femenina con IA, que integra datos personales de móviles, tarjetas de crédito, GPS y pulseras.

La agitada vida de Clark es una muestra de la compleja combinación de habilidad social, amistades peligrosas, inteligencia y resistencia que se necesita para hacer una larga carrera en el sector tecnológico actual.

Un célebre agente literario, John Brockman, fue quien la presentó a Epstein en 2011: “Deberías quedar para cenar con mis niñas, Cami y Michelle. Están en Los Ángeles, consiguiendo dinero para una peli porno enfocada al mercado femenino”, escribió Brockman. Entonces Clark le mandó su móvil e invitó a cenar a Epstein. Un año después fue cuando intentó conseguir el dinero para su proyecto porno, que al principio Epstein no recordaba. “No puedo hacer sexo para la tele”, fue la respuesta final del pedófilo.

Anthropic se presenta en el mundo de la IA como el laboratorio prudente, que antepone la seguridad al ritmo comercial. Amodei ha construido su perfil advirtiendo de los riesgos catastróficos de la IA, hasta el punto de enfrentarse al Pentágono y Trump por la vigilancia masiva y armas autónomas. Esta imagen quedará ahora algo tocada con las revelaciones sobre su mujer.

En 2014, Clark conoció a Amodei y empezaron su relación. Entonces Amodei era un investigador postdoctoral en la Universidad de Stanford, que entró en OpenAI solo en 2016. Clark había sido pareja de Eric Schmidt, entonces presidente ejecutivo de Google, entre 2011 y 2014. Schmidt, 25 años mayor que ella y casado en una conocida relación abierta, fue quien presentó a la pareja. Schmidt fue también uno de los primeros inversores en Anthropic cuando Amodei, su hermana y otros ingenieros dejaron OpenAI para crear la nueva empresa.

Desde entonces, según los medios estadounidenses, Clark se ha convertido en una de las principales asesoras privadas y defensora de Amodei. Su capacidad social ha acercado a Amodei a algunos de los grandes inversores de Silicon Valley. Poco después de la prohibición de Mythos Preview por parte de la Casa Blanca, Clark comió con Ivanka Trump en una conferencia a la que asistió con su marido.

World.title: Shell and Philips hit by Russian ransomware attack
World.content:
The Russia-linked ransomware group Cl0p claims to have hacked global corporations Shell and Philips. The two are among nearly 50 companies Cl0p has listed on its website, alongside General Electric and payments firm Fiserv.

From the oil giant, the group says it has taken some 89 gigabytes of material, including technical drawings, facility images, scans of test reports and project plans. They claimed to have stolen another 13.5 gigabytes from health technology company Philips, mostly diagrams and blueprints.

Both companies are investigating, with Shell saying it is “aware of a possible incident”.

Philips said it had “identified and contained an attempted cybersecurity compromise of a specific enterprise server related to internal data”. A spokesperson told NOS that the incident is now under control and has no impact on its customers.

Russian hackers

Cl0p, which has been active since 2019, is a Russia-linked ransomware group that has likely already extorted $500 million from other victims.

It operates by stealing files and other sensitive data from companies and then threatens to publish them online unless a ransom is paid.

There’s no word yet on how much money the hackers are asking for in exchange for not selling or releasing the stolen data.

Security researchers have linked the campaign to a flaw in Windchill, engineering software made by American firm PTC, which was patched on June 17. Neither Shell nor Philips has said how it was breached.

Writing about the attacks, TNW editor-in-chief Ana-Maria Stanciuc said the pattern carried an uncomfortable lesson: “When enough of the corporate world standardises on the same enterprise platform, one shared supplier quietly becomes everyone’s single point of failure, and no amount of internal security spending can fully patch a hole in someone else’s code.”

World.title: Jetten tells farmers to get off motorways after two die in crash
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has said it is “unacceptable” that tractors were driving on the A59 motorway on Friday, after two people were killed and six injured in a crash. The collision happened at the back of a queue that had built up as the tractors drove to a protest in Den Bosch.

“It is unacceptable and incomprehensible to demonstrate on the motorway because it leads to very dangerous situations,” Jetten said during a press conference.

Jetten also said the decision not to stop the tractors earlier was not a good signal and would have to be reviewed. News agency ANP reported that 50 tractors were driving on the A2 towards Utrecht as he spoke. “Don’t do it, get off the motorway,” Jetten said.

Police said four cars were involved and that they were still investigating what caused the collision, but no tractors were involved.

The victims have not been identified. The tractors had been in the right-hand lane and other traffic could pass on the left, but a traffic jam still built up.

Disputed agreements

Tractors are not permitted on Dutch motorways. Earlier this week the public prosecution department (OM) and the police said they would not stop farmers who drove onto them, citing the right to demonstrate.

A spokesperson for the OM in Oost-Brabant told broadcaster NOS that this had not been agreed. The authorities help demonstrations go ahead, the spokesperson said, but once a tractor is on the motorway it is up to the local mayor, police and prosecutors to decide when and how to step in.

“A tractor on the motorway is never allowed, and is a criminal offence” the spokesperson said. The OM did not answer questions from NOS about what had been agreed instead, or why nobody intervened.

Provincial council members held a minute’s silence for the two dead. Mark van den Oever of Farmers Defence Force called on farmers at the provincial offices not to travel home by motorway.

What the protest is about

Noord-Brabant’s provincial executive intends to revoke the nature permits of five poultry farms close to protected nature areas, after environmental groups won a court case in April 2025.

The court found the protected areas were overloaded with nitrogen, and that the farms were a significant cause. But it stopped short of ordering the permits withdrawn, giving the province, the farmers and the environmental groups a year to come up with a plan that would cut nitrogen levels for good.

The farmers sent in their plans in November 2025 but in July were told their permits would be revoked, although that decision is not yet final. The provincial executive has admitted it never gave them a proper response to those plans, Omroep Brabant reported.

Members of the provincial council, which oversees the executive, broke off their summer break on Friday for a debate on the plan demanded by seven opposition parties, led by farmers’ party BBB. Saskia Boelema, the executive member responsible, told them the province should have sat down with the farmers earlier and apologised for the way the process had been handled.

World.title: Mouse invasion plagues Friesland farmers
World.content:
A mouse plague has been destroying fields in Friesland in the northwest of the country, depleting crops as the rodents eat entire patches of land.

According to Omrop Fryslân, recent weeks have seen the mice mostly causing damage in peat meadows, but they have now also infiltrated clay areas.

“They eat the roots and then the grass dies,” farmer Jan Brouwer from Koufurderrige told the broadcaster. He estimates that it reduces his grass yield by up to 20%.

Drought

The outbreak comes on the heels of a countrywide drought, which has also affected the farmers.

But as there’s no irrigation ban in Friesland yet as compared to other areas of the country, Brouwer was able to flood his fields to flush out the mice. The critters drown in their burrows, and those that try to escape are easy prey for birds.

The water has also helped his land come back to life. “We were making silage today and the grass is starting to come back quite nicely in those spots,” said Brouwer.

The nearby Ijsselmeer still has plenty of water, but that could change if the drought persists.

There have been several mouse plagues since 2015 in the region. And with them, comes an owl invasion, including the short-eared owl. “I have seen at least six short-eared owls here in the past few weeks,” says Brouwer.

Researchers expect the number of mice to decrease substantially next year. “With such a plague, at a certain point there are simply too many,” said Niek Bosma of the regional waterboard. “Then a disease sets in, and within a few weeks all those mice are dead.”

But a few ultimately remain, meaning another mouse plague is inevitable.

World.title: Care homes, prisons and asylum centres hit by night-time heat
World.content:
As daytime temperatures continue to soar during the Netherlands’ fifth heatwave this year, night-time heat, where temperatures stay above 20 degrees, has lagged behind in public discourse despite its effects on the population.

“Night-time heat is an under-examined aspect of heatwaves,” Lisette Klok, researcher at the Climate Adaptation Services foundation, told broadcaster NOS and NRC.

Especially for vulnerable people – including the elderly and those living in asylum seeker centres and prisons – “night-time temperature is important because your body needs the chance to recover from the heat at night. Poor sleep [due to the heat] makes that more difficult.”

Hot nights, which are defined from 11pm to 7am, affect how well people are able to cope during daytime heat. People tend to sleep worse, making them less functional during the day. In addition, homes build up heat because they can’t cool down during the night, meaning neither do their inhabitants.

Climate atlas

The foundation puts out the Climate Impact Atlas, which maps climate effects – from threats of flooding, waterlogging, drought and heat – throughout the country. Using the Atlas, NRC and regional broadcasters found that on average, there are some six tropical nights per year in the Netherlands, although there are regional differences.

Going neighborhood by neighborhood, the journalists found that in parts of South Limburg, there is an average of 15 “sticky nights” annually.

Maastricht has the most hot nights in the country, while the Randstad also has a higher number. The north of the Netherlands sees less than the national average. Urban areas also take a heat hit, with city centres becoming “heat islands” on hot days. Heat in these areas is even worse at night.

“As a result, homes can be cooled less effectively by ventilation,” said Marjolein van Esch, urban microclimate researcher at TU Delft. “This depends on the difference in air temperature between indoors and outdoors. The greater that difference, the easier it is to cool. Due to the urban heat island effect, that temperature difference is smaller.”

Elderly

The high night-time temperatures have a particularly strong effect on older people, who are more vulnerable to heat.

That led some nursing homes being evacuated earlier this summer, including the De Taling care home in Den Bosch and a facility in Raalte whose systems temporarily failed in July.

“Many buildings are designed for a different climate,” a spokesperson for the care organization Carinova told NOS. “The climate systems were tested to the limit at some locations this summer.”

Temporary portable air conditioners and moving residents to cooler rooms helped ease the problems.

Asylum seekers and prisoners

Since 2021, new homes must meet certain requirements to prevent overheating, but the rules don’t apply to existing houses and also usually not to care homes, prisons and asylum seeker centres. Requirements also vary depending on the region.

But residents of asylum seeker centres and prisons, who have nowhere else to go, are not allowed to install air conditioners on their own. Refugee settlement agency COA allows only one fan per room.

According to NRC, the Dutch Correctional Institutions Agency said increasing temperatures in prisons in recent years mean it needs more resources to cool things down. “Many buildings are due for major maintenance or renovation.”

Ajax and Twente both reached the play-off round of the Conference League on Thursday, despite drawing both away games.

Ajax drew 2-2 away at Shelbourne in Dublin, going through 5-3 on aggregate after winning the first leg 3-1 in Amsterdam.

The Amsterdam side led twice in the first half, the second time through Anton Gaaei, but the Irish club equalised on both occasions. Substitute Sean Moore scored the second in the closing stages.

Twente had the easier night, leading 6-0 from the first leg, they drew 3-3 away at DAC 1904 in Slovakia to go through 9-3.

NEC chase Champions League

Every result in Europe counts towards the Uefa coefficient, the ranking that decides how many Dutch clubs qualify each season. The Eredivisie lost sixth place on the Uefa coefficient to Portugal in March, costing it a direct Champions League spot from 2027.

NEC, meanwhile, play Bodø/Glimt on August 19 for a place in the Champions League league phase.

The Conference League draw is on August 28.

World.title: Fifth heatwave confirmed as temperatures reach 37°
World.content:
Temperatures will reach 37° on Friday, after forecaster Weeronline confirmed the fifth regional heatwave of the year.

Temperatures will range from 33° in the north to 37° in the south and southeast, the national weather service KNMI said.

Five heatwaves in a single year have happened only once before, in 1947. Then it was Maastricht alone – this year several southern stations have reached the tally.

There will be no national heatwave, which is measured at the KNMI station in De Bilt, near Utrecht. Most of the country, including the Randstad and the north, will fall below the threshold.

KNMI has issued a code yellow warning for heat across the country. The national heat plan, run by public health institute RIVM, puts care homes and health services on alert. It covers the whole country on Friday and only the southeast on Saturday.

Friday night will stay warm, with temperatures holding near 20° in towns and cities.

Saturday will be cooler, with a chance of thunderstorms, although the southeast may still reach about 32°. Sunday will peak at 24°, and next week will be cooler and wetter, with maximums of 21 to 25° and rain likely from Tuesday.

The weekend rain will do little for the drought. Weeronline says short showers run off ground that is baked too hard to absorb water.

World.title: Illegal gambling ads on Meta target vulnerable gamblers: BNR
World.content:
Unlicensed gambling sites are running adverts on Facebook and Instagram that target vulnerable people who have signed themselves onto the national register barring them from gambling, an investigation by radio station BNR has found.

More than 100,000 people in the Netherlands have registered with Cruks, the self-exclusion scheme set up when online gambling was legalised, which requires every licensed casino, arcade and betting site to turn them away.

BNR found that searching Facebook for terms such as “Cruks”, geen Cruks or zonder Cruks (without Cruks) – surfaces a stream of adverts from casinos that hold no Dutch licence, promising large bonuses and offering routes around the register.

The adverts follow a consistent pattern, BNR reported: they suggest Cruks is restricting the user, then point them towards unlicensed alternatives. One features an AI-generated woman who tells viewers that international casinos do not consult the Dutch register and invites them to play the same day.

The accounts placing them carry names such as Betrouwbare Spelsites (reliable gaming sites). Users who encounter the adverts on Facebook go on to see them on Instagram and Threads.

Addiction specialists told BNR they were concerned that people registered with Cruks were being singled out, because seeing gambling adverts can trigger strong urges in addicts.

Meta removed adverts

Meta pulled a large number of the adverts from its public ad library after BNR put questions to the company, and the accounts that were identified were taken offline.

In a written response, Meta said it takes enforcement seriously and that advertisers must comply with the law. It declined to tell BNR what it earns from the adverts.

An estimate published in May by two gambling industry bodies KVA and VNLOK put Meta’s annual revenue from illegal gambling adverts aimed at the Netherlands at between €7.3 million and €13.6 million.

The figure is modelled from publicly available advertising data rather than confirmed by Meta, and the report states that it is not suggesting Meta knowingly allows the adverts.

VNLOK took Meta to court in June in an attempt to force it to act faster, and complained to the European Commission that the company is not meeting its obligations under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

The cabinet set out plans in June for a complete ban on online gambling advertising and bonuses. Junior justice minister Claudia van Bruggen has said the rise in gambling addiction, particularly among young people, is deeply worrying.

If you are concerned about your own or someone else’s gambling, OpenOverGokken, the national gambling helpline run by regulator the Kansspelautoriteit, can be reached free on 0800 24 000 22, day or night.

World.title: Man admits bomb attack on D66 office, calls it protest
World.content:
The man who set off a firework bomb at the D66 headquarters in The Hague in May has admitted the attack, telling a court it was a protest against Dutch asylum policy and what he called the dismantling of the country.

The 37-year-old, identified as Berry van D., appeared at a preliminary hearing at The Hague district court on Thursday. He is accused of causing an explosion with terrorist intent.

About 30 people, most of them members of the party’s youth wing, were inside the building when the firework bomb went off shortly after 9pm. No one was hurt.

Van D. said he had not known anyone was there because he had seen no lights on and that he never intended to hurt anyone.

Prosecutors said he acted alone and told the court he had a political message and wanted to silence people who think differently, ANP reported.

Van D. was arrested about an hour after the blast in the Grote Marktstraat, the city’s main shopping street, carrying two knives. NOS reported that he has a previous conviction for setting fire to city buses in Tilburg, where he had worked as a driver.

He told the court he had turned to violence because voting and peaceful demonstration had achieved nothing.

Psychiatric assessment

Thursday’s hearing was procedural and no trial date has been set yet. Van D. will be transferred to a forensic psychiatric clinic to assess whether he can be held responsible for his actions.

NOS reported that Van D. presents himself on social media as a supporter of the anti-immigration PVV, and described D66 leader Rob Jetten being sworn in as prime minister in February as a black day for the country.

The office on the Lange Houtstraat was also attacked in September last year, when rioters from an anti-immigration demonstration smashed its windows.

Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). These will allow investment assets such as shares and investment fund units to be exempt from the 19% capital gains tax up to a limit of 100,000 zloty. Of this amount, up to 25,000 zloty may be held in savings assets such as bonds and deposits. Assets held in an OKI above those limits will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has only a majority of nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years

Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. The personal data of almost 19 million people, including medical information, has been compromised in a major cyberattack on a company that provides services to thousands of medical facilities in Poland. “We are dealing with one of the largest incidents in Poland’s history,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on Wednesday. He urged people to use government services to check whether their data is affected and to “lock” their national identity number to prevent potential fraud. (￼🧵 1/2) 💬 Dziś doszło do poważnego wycieku danych w firmie MyDr, który może obejmować blisko 19 milionów osób korzystających z opieki medycznej. W związku z sytuacją krytyczną zostały natychmiast podjęte działania mające zabezpieczyć dane i wyjaśnić okoliczności incydentu –… pic.twitter.com/nIp6EvbKiu — Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji (@CYFRA_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The attack targeted MyDr, a company that provides services used by many medical facilities in Poland. Its data includes patients’ personal information, as well as medical details such as diagnoses and prescriptions. It was first reported on Monday by Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service, which said that it had been contacted on Saturday by the alleged perpetrators, who claimed to have accessed the data of around 18.8 million people. The hackers, who have not been identified, had also sent a screenshot from the compromised database showing the personal data of “one of the most important politicians in Poland”, added Zaufana Trzecia Strona. Shortly afterwards, MyDr confirmed that it had “become the target of an external, deliberate criminal activity involving some of our data”. In an update on Wednesday, it said that, at the time of writing, there was no evidence that the data had been published anywhere. Największy wyciek danych osobowych w historii Polski i co możemy z nim zrobić – nasza analiza incydentu w MyDr i jego potencjalnych skutków.https://t.co/vXUmVfpPAP Opisujemy aktualny stan wiedzy i możliwe scenariusze rozwoju sytuacji. pic.twitter.com/uqhjz1CjZ1 — ZaufanaTrzeciaStrona @zaufanatrzeciastrona@infosec (@Zaufana3Strona) August 13, 2026 Gawkowski addressed the issue at a press briefing on Wednesday. He noted that “there is no indication we are dealing with an external attack…from Russia or any other country”. Poland has recently regularly been targetted by Russian state-linked hackers. It is “very likely” that cybercriminals are behind the attack on MyDr, said Gawkowski, who pledged that there would be an “uncompromising” response from the Polish security services. The minister advised Poles to check in a secure government database whether their data had been leaked. He also advised citizens to use the state web portal, known as mObywatel, to “lock” their identity number, known as a PESEL, which prevents fraudsters from using it. Around 12,000 medical facilities use MyDr’s services, the digital affairs ministry told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The company claims that it processes three million medical consultations and 2.7 million prescriptions a month, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. World.title: Fugitive Polish opposition politician reportedly in pro-Russian Moldovan breakaway region

A letter sent to a Polish court by Marcin Romanowski, who served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government and is now on the run from criminal charges, suggests that he is residing in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. The Polish authorities have been trying to locate and extradite Romanowski, whose whereabouts have been unknown since he fled Budapest earlier this year after Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who had granted him asylum, lost power. Były wiceminister sprawiedliwości ma przebywać w Tyraspolu, stolicy zbuntowanej mołdawskiej prowincji znajdującej się pod patronatem Rosji. Spod tego adresu w Naddniestrzu polityk PiS miał wystąpić o wydanie listu żelaznego.https://t.co/m05dtQv3KV — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) August 12, 2026 On Wednesday, following media reports that Romanowski had sent a letter to the Polish authorities from Transnistria, a spokeswoman for Warsaw’s district court, which is responsible for extradition matters, confirmed to news website Gazeta.pl that this was the case. “The letter and envelope indicate that the package was sent to the court from Tiraspol in Transnistria,” said judge Anna Ptaszek. “It bears his handwritten signature.” Przemysław Nowak, the spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, also confirmed to broadcaster RMF that Romanowski had sent the letter, in which he indicated that he was residing in Tiraspol, the capital of Transnistria, and requested safe passage to Poland. The fugitive politician said that he would be willing to appear in court or before prosecutors, on the condition that he was not placed in detention, said Nowak, who added that prosecutors had not yet taken a position on Romanowski’s request. Transnistria is a region of eastern Moldova, bordering Ukraine, that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s, even fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. The territory’s flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Romanowski’s apparent presence in the Russian-linked territory was condemned by figures from Poland’s government. “I would say that Romanowski is now very likely under the influence of Russian intelligence,” said deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. Paweł Wojtunik, the former head of Poland’s Central Anticorruption Bureau (CBA), who previously worked in Moldova, wrote that “it is impossible to enter [Transnistria], let alone to live there, without the consent of the local KGB, which is directly managed by the Russian GRU and FSB [intelligence agences]”. – Dzisiaj powiedziałbym, że Romanowski z dużym prawdopodobieństwem jest pod wpływem rosyjskich służb – ocenił wiceszef MON Cezary Tomczyk. Sprawę skomentował też szef MSZ Radosław Sikorski.https://t.co/LuWw0bkh2j — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 12, 2026 Even a deputy leader of Romanowski’s own party, the national-conservative PiS, was unwilling to defend him. In an interview with Polsat News, Przemysław Czarnek noted that it is still not confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. But he agreed, when asked by the host, that it “would be crossing a line” for Romanowski to be in the territory. Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government between 2019 and 2023. He remains a member of parliament, despite having fled Poland in December 2024 after prosecutors sought to bring charges against him for 11 alleged crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group. Those alleged offences relate to Romanowski’s time at the justice ministry, which was then led by Zbigniew Ziobro, who is also wanted on multiple charges. Both Romanowski and Ziobro obtained asylum in Hungary when the country was led by PiS-ally Orbán. The Polish government says that Hungary has revoked the refugee status and travel documents granted to fugitive ex-justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro by Viktor Orbán. Poland will now seek Ziobro's deportation from the US, where he fled after leaving Hungary https://t.co/TcVw0AiEMX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 However, after Orbán lost power earlier this year, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains. Last month, Poland requested his extradition, though that is a process that could take years. Romanowski, meanwhile, disappeared completely, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians have denied the allegations against them and have claimed to be victims of “political revenge” by the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk that took power in December 2023. They have argued that they would not be able to receive a fair trial in Poland while Tusk remains in power because of the government’s influence over the judicial system. On Wednesday, Romanowski’s lawyer, Bartosz Lewandowski, confirmed that his client had requested safe passage to Poland and that he was “outside the territory of the European Union”. However, he did not confirm that Romanowski is in Transnistria. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
