World.title: Popular Lebanese restaurant Al Beiruti to open in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Al Beiruti, a popular Lebanese restaurant, is set to build its first Iraqi branch in Iraq Mall in Baghdad, adding another significant regional dining name to the capital’s growing restaurant scene.

The Baghdad inauguration will be the next chapter of Al Beiruti’s regional development, after previous launches in Jordan and Qatar, as well as its established presence in the UAE.

The restaurant announced that its Iraq Mall restaurant is about to open, with a local franchise arrangement handling the expansion.

Al Beiruti has become a renowned location for Lebanese food in the Middle East, providing both classic dishes and a more modern restaurant experience.

The menu includes Lebanese favorites, including manakish, fattoush, hummus, baba ghanouj, and grilled halloumi, as well as shawarma, wraps, and mixed grills. Larger meals include steak, chicken escalope, and grilled salmon.

Al Beiruti joins a growing number of international and regional food and beverage companies in Baghdad, as new malls and commercial expansions change the city’s retail and entertainment markets.

Iraq Mall has emerged as a focal point of that expansion, drawing new restaurants, boutiques, and entertainment ideas as consumer spending and private-sector investment continue to rise in the capital.

World.title: Baghdad and Erbil agree on unified digital customs system across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Baghdad and Erbil have agreed to fully adopt the digital ASYCUDA customs system across border crossings, with non-oil border earnings shared equally by the federal and Kurdistan regional governments.

The deal is a significant step toward standardizing customs processes across Iraq and addressing long-standing disagreements over border revenues and claimed import quantities.

ASYCUDA, designed by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), digitizes customs declarations, payments, and clearing processes, allowing authorities to better monitor products entering the nation and the income they earn.

Linking customs operations to Iraq’s banking and electronic payment systems may help limit the potential for underreporting, revenue leakage, and corruption at border crossings.

The deal comes as Iraq’s Finance Ministry and Central Bank work to digitize customs, payments, and government financial data in collaboration with UNCTAD.

A combined computerized customs system for Baghdad and Erbil might give more accurate revenue data while resolving one of the two governments’ ongoing financial issues.

The change is also significant for Iraq’s overall economy.

More open and uniform customs processes might facilitate cross-border commerce, boost governmental revenues, and enhance the business climate as Iraq pursues more foreign investment and closer integration with international markets.

World.title: Iraq’s Chief Justice Faiq Zidan meets Syrian President Al-Sharaa in Damascus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus on Thursday, marking another high-level Iraqi outreach to a neighboring Arab state as Baghdad seeks to bolster regional relations under rising security problems.

Al-Sharaa welcomed Zidan and an Iraqi delegation to the People’s Palace, which also included Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Justice Minister Mazhar al-Wais.

According to the Syrian president, the talks focused on extending judicial and legal cooperation between Iraq and Syria, as well as resolving mutual concerns.

The visit also resulted in more practical conversations among the two nations’ judicial officials. Iraqi and Syrian authorities agreed to set up joint judicial committees to continue working on cases involving Syrian prisoners and other cross-border legal issues.

Zidan’s visit is crucial as he is one of the most prominent persons in Iraq’s state institutions, and it coincides with Baghdad’s increased diplomatic, security, and judicial interaction with its neighbors.

The Damascus meetings come after a separate Iraqi security group visited Riyadh, where senior military official Abdul Amir al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman.

Zidan had also just visited Ankara as part of a larger Iraqi effort to build ties with Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Turkey.

That approach has become more urgent in light of the regional escalation involving Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

In late July, the United States and Saudi Arabia conducted synchronized attacks against locations used by Iran-aligned organizations in Iraq, after Riyadh accused militias operating from Iraqi territory of firing drones against Saudi energy infrastructure.

The incident put Baghdad under strong pressure to prevent armed organizations from exploiting Iraqi territory to launch assaults on neighboring nations and also highlighted the potential that militia activity may harm Iraq’s improved ties with Arab governments.

Against this setting, Zidan’s encounter with Al-Sharaa is significant beyond regular court cooperation.

Iraq and Syria share a long border and confront shared concerns such as terrorism, organized crime, prisoners, and cross-border security. Baghdad also has a strategic interest in preserving stable ties with Damascus, as Iraq strives to boost regional connections and prevent unrest from spilling over its borders.

Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration sees recent diplomatic efforts as part of a larger effort to strengthen Iraq’s ties with its neighbors while keeping the nation out of the developing conflict between Iran and its regional adversaries.

Baghdad has increasingly emphasized that choices on security, armament, and relations with neighboring governments must be made by Iraqi official authorities rather than armed groupings.

The travels to Damascus and Riyadh therefore convey an essential message: although Iran-aligned militias have exacerbated tensions between Iraq and certain of its neighbors, Iraqi official institutions are working directly with those nations to restore cooperation and avoid further escalation.

Strengthening judicial, diplomatic, and security ties with Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey might serve as an essential regional buffer for Iraq as it seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, control armed groups, and avoid being drawn further into the region’s crises.

World.title: Iraq’s Al-Shammari visits Riyadh to meet Saudi Defense Minister
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A top Iraqi security team has traveled to Riyadh for meetings with Saudi Arabia’s leadership, as Baghdad and the Kingdom work to improve security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

First Lieutenant General Abdul Amir Al-Shammari, director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman on Thursday to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

According to reports from the visit, the conversations included cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration.

The conference is especially significant in light of the combined US-Saudi attacks on Iran-linked militia locations in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

The strikes drastically escalated tensions between Baghdad and Riyadh, highlighting the Iraqi government’s problems in preventing armed groups from exploiting its territory to target neighboring nations.

Thursday’s visit indicates that both parties are now attempting to move beyond that conflict via direct military and intelligence collaboration.

Prince Khalid underlined Saudi Arabia’s commitment to Iraq’s security, stability, and economic growth, identifying it as an essential neighbor with whom the Kingdom has strong political and social relations.

The meetings in Riyadh follow Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali al-Humaidan’s visit to Baghdad last week, during which he met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and reiterated an offer for the Iraqi leader to visit Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad’s security cooperation with Riyadh has grown more vital as the government seeks to prevent Iran-backed militias from drawing Iraq into a larger regional conflict.

Al-Zaidi has frequently said that Iraqi soil should not be used to attack other nations and has stepped up efforts for weaponry to be put solely under state control.

The most recent Iraqi trip to Riyadh symbolizes more than just normal defense diplomacy. It is part of a joint effort by Baghdad and Saudi Arabia to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into conflict.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: Village defence guard kills another in Udhampur; 1 critical
World.content:
JAMMU: A village defence guard (VDG) was killed Friday and another critically injured after a colleague allegedly opened fire following a brawl in J&Kâs Udhampur, officials said.

The fratricide unfolded in Damnote area Udhampurâs Panchari around 10am when Surjeet Singh turned the gun on his colleagues during the spat.

âIn a fit of anger, one of the VDGs fired on his colleagues. The shooting resulted in the death of VDG Baldev Singh and left Ramesh Singh injured,â an official said. He added that early preliminary probe indicated the attack arose out of personal enmity.

World.title: BJP MP served notice for duties he no longer holds
World.content:

Jodhpur: In an embarrassing mix-up, Jodhpur zila parishad's chief executive officer, in his capacity as district election officer, Thursday issued a notice to Member of Parliament Manna Lal Rawat for negligence in election duties, mistakenly believing the latter still held a position as joint commissioner with the state transport department.The notice, which warned Rawat of potential disciplinary action due to a failure to update the list of his subordinate employees on the state govt's EMS (employee management system) portal in preparation for the upcoming municipal elections, was swiftly retracted following public ridicule on social media Friday.Rawat, who resigned from his state govt post prior to the 2024 general elections, is currently serving as a Lok Sabha member representing Udaipur on a BJP ticket. The goof-up occurred as a govt portal was not updated. Confirming this, Rawat said that district election officer (CEO, zila parishad) Ashish Kumar Mishra called him, admitted the mistake and withdrew the notice.Rawat was earlier posted as the transport department's joint commissioner in Jodhpur. He took voluntary retirement in 2024 to contest the parliamentary elections that year. Despite his retirement and subsequent election as a public representative, Rawat's name continued to figure in the list of govt employees maintained by the Jodhpur district election authorities.The error came to light after the notice was issued to him, raising questions over the way employee data is maintained and updated by the state election machinery. "It is surprising and worrisome," said Rawat, adding that despite the govt machinery operating in a digital environment, election-related data was still carrying information that was nearly three years old. Rawat questioned how govt departments were maintaining the data of ordinary citizens and serving employees if the records of a retired senior govt officer had not been removed from the list even after a considerable lapse of time.

World.title: Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart
World.content:
Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a statewide inspection drive uncovered multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The August 13 drive covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale and delivery of food through online platforms. The FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations, news agency PTI reported.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd.The inspections focused on storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management, personal hygiene of food handlers, food safety records, display of licences and compliance with inventory practices such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food items stored beyond their declared "use by" dates.The regulator also flagged unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in personal hygiene, adding that the company's response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices.In Mumbai, a Blinkit facility in Malad (West) was found to be operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. Inspectors also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations and that records were unavailable.The FDA said several workers were not using protective gear such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Inspectors also found damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate segregation of different categories of food products.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, officials flagged shortcomings in drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet was classified as non-compliant after scoring 46 per cent during the inspection.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon revealed deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display.At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and deficiencies in hygiene and temperature control.The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.At a Blinkit store in Karad in Satara district, officials checked 125 delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records. The regulator also found that the outlet's FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery bags and boxes.The FDA directed the company to suspend two-wheeler delivery operations at the outlet until the deficiencies were addressed.The regulator said the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and urged all food businesses operating through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed food safety, hygiene and storage standards.

World.title: BMS calls nationwide protests on Aug 17 over pension, wages and labour codes
World.content:
The organisation has asked all its units across the country to hold demonstrations, rallies and dharnas

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS) has called for nationwide protests on August 17 over a range of pending labour issues, including higher minimum pension, revision of EPF and ESI wage ceilings, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme and changes to provisions of the new labour codes.The organisation has asked all its units across the country to hold demonstrations, rallies and dharnas at district headquarters and submit memorandums to the Prime Minister, finance minister and labour minister. A major protest is planned at Jantar Mantar in Delhi from 10am, with workers and representatives of BMS-affiliated unions and federations expected to participate.Among its key demands, BMS has sought an increase in the minimum pension under EPS-95 to Rs 7,500 a month and its linkage with variable dearness allowance and Ayushman Bharat. It has also demanded that the ESI wage ceiling be doubled from Rs 21,000 to Rs 42,000 and the EPF ceiling raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000.The union has sought bonus on full wages in line with the new labour codes, an increase in the wage ceiling used for bonus calculation and gratuity based on 30 days' wages instead of 15 days, without any upper limit. It has also demanded inflation-linked minimum wages, higher honorarium for anganwadi, ASHA, mid-day meal and other scheme workers, and equal pay for contract and outsourced workers doing the same work.Other demands include a five-day work week in banks, filling vacancies in government services and public establishments, convening the Indian Labour Conference and restoring OPS.BMS has also reiterated its opposition to several provisions of the Industrial Relations Code and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, arguing that they could weaken workers' rights, job security and social security. It has sought formal consultations between the Centre and central trade unions before amendments are made.The organisation also wants the Centre and states to reconsider the status of more than one crore âscheme workersâ, saying many work 10-12 hours a day but remain outside effective labour-law and social-security protection.

World.title: Govt scraps 12-minute ad cap for TV channel
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Television channels will no longer be restricted to 12 minutes of s per hour, with the government deciding to scrap the two-decade-old cap in a move it says will put traditional broadcasters on a more level footing with digital platforms.The restriction, introduced in 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, will cease to apply once the amended rules are notified in the Gazette, the information and broadcasting ministry said.The government has argued that the television landscape has changed substantially since the cap was imposed. India had only 62 TV channels in 2006, compared with more than 900 now. Cable television, then the dominant distribution platform, was largely analog and offered limited capacity and consumer choice.With digitisation, platforms including cable TV, direct-to-home, HITS and IPTV can now carry 300 to 500 channels or more, significantly expanding viewer choice and competition, the ministry said.The decision could give broadcasters greater flexibility to determine advertising inventory, an important consideration for an industry that remains heavily dependent on advertising revenue across both pay and free-to-air channels.The ministry also cited the growing competition television faces from digital media, where there is no comparable statutory cap on advertising duration.It said the existing restriction had created a ânon-level playing fieldâ for conventional television broadcasters and that removing it would promote âfair competitionâ and ease of doing business.The change, however, will become operational only from the date the amendment to the Cable Television Networks Rules is formally notified.

World.title: President Murmu approves 78 gallantry awards
World.content:
NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday approved 78 gallantry awards, including 13 posthumous, to defence forces and central armed police forces personnel on the eve of the 80th

.

The awards are 9 Kirti Chakras, including 7 posthumous; 1 Bar to Shaurya Chakra; 19 Shaurya Chakras, including one posthumous; 5 Bar to Sena Medals (gallantry); 36 Sena Medals (gallantry), including 5 posthumous; 3 Nao Sena Medal (gallantry); and 5 Vayu Sena Medals (gallantry).

Kirti Chakra is India's second-highest peacetime gallantry award after Ashoka Chakra. Shaurya Chakra is the third-highest peacetime gallantry award.

The Kirti Chakra awardees are Lt Col Manoj Francis of 21 Para (Special Forces) and Major Jitendra Rathee of 2 Para (Special Forces). Seven other Kirti Chakras were conferred posthumously.

The armed forces personnel granted the prestigious awards posthumously included Havildar Gajendra Singh of 2 Para (Special Forces); Head Constables Jagbir Singh and Bashir Ahmad; Constables Jaswant Singh, Balvinder Singh and Tariq Hussain; and Inspector Sunil Kumar.

World.title: Pew survey: What US, UK and others think about India at 80
World.content:
At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.



Neighbourhood contrasts & global scorecard

as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?

India's image is changing

Politics matters too

A mixed but largely positive global image

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As India completes 79 years of independence, its global standing presents a striking study in contrasts.A Pew Research Center survey conducted across 36 countries between February and May 2026 reveals an international community divided down the middle: a global median of 45% of respondents hold a favorable view of India, while 41% express an unfavorable opinion.Behind this median lies a complex tapestry of geopolitical shifts, historical rivalries, and evolving regional alliances.From enthusiasm in Western Europe and East Africa to frosty hostility in parts of the Middle East and South Asia, public perception of the worldâs most populous democracy depends heavily on where you ask.Nowhere is this divergence more intense than in India's immediate backyard. While proximity can foster cooperation, in South Asia it has produced antithetical attitudes.Sri Lanka has the most favourable view of India, with 79% of adults expressing a positive opinion.Pakistan sits at the opposite end, with just 7% viewing India favourably. The gulf between the two countries reflects decades of conflict, political rivalry and competing national narratives.Turkey is another major outlier. Only 15% of Turks have a favourable opinion of India, while a majority hold an unfavourable view.In the West Bank and East Jerusalem, just 18% express a positive opinion.Yet beyond these pockets of hostility, India finds considerable goodwill across much of the world.Kenya and the United Kingdom rank alongside Sri Lanka among the countries most positive towards India, with roughly seven in 10 adults expressing favourable views.Majorities in Germany, Israel, Italy, Sweden, Japan and Thailand also see India positively.In contrast, Latin American publics express mixed-to-negative views, alongside substantial shares of respondents who offer no opinion.The findings suggest that India's global image is not simply a reflection of its diplomatic alliances.Economic ties, strategic partnerships, cultural familiarity and perceptions of India's growing global role all appear to shape how people view the country.The bigger story is perhaps not where India stands today, but how its image has changed.In most countries surveyed, opinions have remained relatively stable since Pew last asked the question. But in 10 countries, the change has been statistically significant â and in seven of them, India's favourability has fallen.Turkey and Nigeria have recorded the sharpest declines since 2025, with the share of people expressing a favourable opinion of India falling by 10 percentage points in both countries.India has also lost ground in the United States, Indonesia, South Africa and Mexico.The decline is particularly striking in Bangladesh.Pew's previous survey there was conducted in 2024. Since then, the share of Bangladeshis with a favourable opinion of India has fallen by 15 percentage points, leaving fewer than half with a positive view.At the same time, the number of Bangladeshis who do not express an opinion has also fallen sharply, from 24% to just 7%. In other words, more Bangladeshis now appear to have a defined opinion of India â and that opinion has become considerably less favourable.The trend is not uniformly negative, however.India's image has improved significantly in Germany, Britain and Sri Lanka.The share of Britons with a favourable opinion of India has risen 11 points since 2025, while Germany has recorded a six-point increase. Sri Lanka has seen an even bigger jump, with favourability rising 14 points since 2024.Looking further back to 2023 reveals another interesting divide.Across several European countries, India's image has strengthened substantially since the first post-pandemic survey. In Germany, for example, only 47% had a favourable opinion of India in 2023. That figure has now climbed to 63%.France has followed a similar trajectory. India's favourability there has risen from 39% in 2023 to 50% today.Outside Europe, however, the picture is less encouraging.South Korea is one example. In 2023, 59% of South Koreans viewed India favourably. Today, that figure has dropped to 44%.Latin America also tends to lean more negative, although large numbers of people in several European and Latin American countries do not express an opinion at all.India's global image is also shaped by domestic political ideology in some countries.The United States and Canada show a striking pattern: people on the political left are more likely than conservatives to view India favourably.In the US, 54% of liberals express a positive opinion of India, compared with 40% of conservatives. In Canada, the corresponding figures are 58% and 45%.Israel presents almost the exact opposite picture.There, 68% of people on the political right view India favourably, compared with just 46% on the left.The ideological divide underlines how perceptions of India can be tied not only to India's own policies, but also to how different political constituencies interpret its role in the world.So, as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?The answer is neither uniformly celebratory nor overwhelmingly negative.Pakistan and Turkey may give India the stink eye, but they represent the more hostile end of a much broader spectrum.From Sri Lanka and Kenya to Britain, Germany and Israel, India enjoys strong positive sentiment in several strategically important countries.At the same time, the declines in Bangladesh, the US, South Korea, Turkey, Nigeria and other countries show that India's global image cannot be taken for granted.India's international reputation is therefore becoming more consequential â and more contested.As New Delhi seeks a larger role in global affairs, its challenge will not simply be to build economic and military power, but also to shape how that power is perceived abroad.At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.

World.title: DDA proposes higher FAR for slum revamp in Master Plan for Delhi-2047
World.content:
Increasing the floor area ratio (FAR) for in situ slum rehabilitation, reducing the minimum plot size for transit-oriented development (TOD) and taking a more proactive role in implementing land pooling are among the changes the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has made in the Master Plan for Delhi-2047.

The plan, approved by the urban body on August 12 and sent to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for clearance, proposes raising the FAR of the rehabilitation component (for EWS housing) for in situ slum projects from 400 to 500 and the remunerative component (for sale in the open market) from 300 to 500. It also removes the existing maximum density restriction for such projects.

FAR is the ratio of a building’s total built-up area to the total area of the plot.

The plan estimates Delhi’s population to rise from about 2.4 crore currently to 3.2 crore by 2047. It identifies 350 sq km as “future urbanisable area” while noting that Delhi is landlocked and has no possibility of “horizontal expansion”.

The plan also proposes allowing commercial activity on residential plots along roads that are at least 30 metres wide, introducing a “24-hour city” concept and a new transferable development rights framework.

Under the proposed mixed-use provisions, commercial activity would be permitted on the ground floor or lower first floor of residential plots on roads with a minimum right of way of 30 metres. Parking would have to be provided within the plot or in common parking facilities, including multi-level parking in the vicinity. The plan also identifies 2,183 mixed-use streets, where commercial activity would be allowed on the ground floor, and 355 commercial streets, where it would be allowed on all floors.

Land pooling

The MPD-2047 retains land pooling as a major development policy covering about 200 sq km.

Around 20,000 hectares have been identified for land pooling across 105 villages, of which the DDA says about 17,000 hectares are vacant and available for development.

Landowners have so far expressed willingness to participate in about 7,865 hectares or 46.3% of the area. Participation varies significantly across zones: 60.1% in P-II, 4.1% in P-I, 55.2% in N, 31.3% in L, 12.8% in K-I and 99.8% in Zone J.

The revised framework proposes a minimum sector size of 20 hectares and a 60:40 land distribution model. It also gives the DDA a more proactive role, including acting on behalf of landowners where consortium formation is difficult. Around 600 km of new roads are proposed in the land-pooling areas, with the urban body developing roads, greens, utilities and public facilities.

Provisions for JJ clusters

The DDA has proposed a two-pronged approach for notified jhuggi-jhopri (JJ) clusters whose population is estimated at about 12 lakh — in-situ rehabilitation under the Jahan Jhuggi Wahan Makan policy and relocation of slums located on ecologically sensitive sites.

A new ‘High Density Corridor’ policy has also been proposed along a 250-metre-wide corridor on either side of Urban Extension Road-II.

For unauthorised colonies, regularisation is proposed on an “as is where is” basis, without requiring a layout plan or minimum road width.

For the Yamuna riverfront, the plan identifies 9,934 hectares as Zone O. Within the active floodplain, it proposes a no-construction zone, allowing only recreational use and utilities. Outside the floodplain, development would remain restricted, alongside ecological restoration, rejuvenation and recreational uses.

The DDA has also proposed a geographic information system-based land-use plan incorporating land pooling, TOD and high-density corridors, along with major infrastructure such as the metro, Regional Rapid Transit System and roads. A Digital Twin of Delhi has been proposed to help regulate encroachment and unauthorised construction.

World.title: Heated exchange between BJP and Priyank Kharge over Bill ‘targeting’ RSS
World.content:
The Karnataka Cabinet clearing a Bill that the BJP claims indirectly targets the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), by making it mandatory for private associations to seek permission to use public spaces, triggered a heated exchange between the saffron party leaders and Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Friday.

Launching an attack on the Home Minister, the BJP dared the government to try banning the RSS, while Mr. Kharge wondered if the RSS was a terrorist/underworld organisation or a group of criminals to threaten those who questioned it.

Responding to media queries on efforts to target the RSS through the Karnataka Regulation of Use of Government Premises and Public Property Bil, likely to be tabled in the ongoing Monsoon Session, BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra said: “Though the name of the RSS has not been directly mentioned in the Bill, it is clear that the Chief Minister and the Home Minister are trying to indirectly target the RSS.”

He said the government should try to ban the RSS “if it has the courage.”

He declared that the BJP would not tolerate any efforts to target the RSS and maintained that the RSS was able to grow strongly though it had been banned earlier. He asked the Congress government to learn from history before making any move with respect to RSS.

In a similar tone, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok asked: “If you continue to focus only on targeting RSS, what will happen at your doorsteps after one-and-a-half years? (when the term of the Assembly ends)?”

Responding strongly to this, Mr. Kharge said that Mr. Ashok’s statement implied that one cannot come out of his house if he takes on the RSS. “Is he implying that the RSS is a terrorist organisation or an underworld mafia that finishes off those who question it? I have the protection from the Constitution to come out of my house and I have the moral courage given by Babasaheb Ambedkar to talk freely.”

Wondering why the BJP felt the Bill only targeted the RSS, he said, “Such anxiety will haunt only those who are guilty.”

World.title: Zoya Hasan’s lecture on pluralism at Delhi school cancelled over ‘security concerns’
World.content:
An Independence Day address on pluralism by Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) Professor Emerita Zoya Hasan at Sardar Patel Vidyalaya was called off at the last minute on Friday over “security concerns”.

According to those aware of the incident, protesters gathered outside the school ahead of the event, where the noted academic was scheduled to speak on ‘Why pluralism is important’, after which police reached the scene. Academics condemned the incident, with some claiming that the protesters were from the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP).

Invited as chief guest

Professor Hasan said she had received a formal invitation from the school principal weeks ago to serve as the chief guest at their Independence Day programme.

She added that a teacher called her at 8.30 a.m. on Friday, saying she was on her way to pick her up.

“Instead, the security head came and informed me that the event had been cancelled because of security concerns,” said Professor Hasan. Sources said the rest of the event was held as planned. When reached for comment, school principal Anuradha Joshi did not respond.

The incident comes days after the JNU administration withdrew permission to hold a discussion on a book by former student Umar Khalid.

In an X post, economist Jayati Ghosh wrote: “When informal pressure on the school from official sources to cancel the programme failed, they resorted to this extreme last-minute measure.”

‘Pressure on school’

DU Professor Apoorvanand said, “Delhi Police should have restrained the lumpens of the VHP, but they forced the school to cancel the talk by Prof. Zoya Hasan.”

Yamini Aiyar, a parent and former president of the Centre for Policy Research, said, “It is ironic that during an Independence Day programme to celebrate the freedom struggle, our own government curbs the school’s freedoms.”

The Delhi police, however, said they were not aware of any gathering or protest at the school.

“After receiving information about the purported event, police visited the school. We made several enquiries and found no evidence of any gathering or protest at the site,” said a senior officer.

World.title: Mahua Moitra alleges she was asked to vacate circuit house late at night
World.content:
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Friday (August 14, 2026) said that she has been directed by the Nadia district administration to vacate the circuit house in Nadia district late in the evening.

Ms. Moitra is a Lok Sabha MP from Krishnanagar in Nadia district.

Huge crowd outside Krishnagar Circuit House shouting "Jai Shree Ram" while district administration calling/messaging me repeatedly to vacate room. Supreme Court asked me to face bullets so here I am … not backing down pic.twitter.com/1o0GmywXg8 — Mahua Moitra (@MahuaMoitra) August 14, 2026

“I entered Circuit House at 18:30 hrs & given same room I always stay in. Dinner was served to me in room at 9:20 pm. I received call at 9:47 asking me to vacate. Now at 10:52 I receive this message with this ‘order’! Outside the gates are huge crowd shouting Jai Shree Ram!,” Ms. Moitra posted on social media.

The MP also shared an order dated August 12 by the Deputy Collector of Nadia district stating that her reservation at the circuit house has been temporarily suspended for annual maintenance.

In a video message, Ms. Moitra stated that as an MP of the district she was entitled to a stay at the circuit house and she was not vacating it as per district administration orders. In her messages, Ms. Moitra repeatedly claimed that a crowd had gathered outside the circuit house chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’.

Leaders from different political parties in the Opposition raised the issue on social media and urged the administration to ensure her security. Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee raised concern that a woman MP was ordered out of the circuit house in the middle of the night.

“And tomorrow, the BJP leaders will stand before the country and speak about women’s empowerment. You cannot celebrate Nari Shakti on a stage and use the power of the State to intimidate a woman who challenges you. That is not authority. That is insecurity @SuvenduWB,” Mr. Banerjee posted on social media, sharing the video message of her party MP.

Congress leader Pawan Khera said a “sitting woman MP is being forced to vacate the circuit house in the middle of the night while there is a baying mob waiting for her outside”. He urged the Chief Minister, the Prime Minister and the Home Minister “to ensure her security and well-being”.

On July 1, Ms. Moitra had faced protests by a mob allegedly comprising Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers at a local party office in Nadia’s Krishnanagar. She claimed that the mob threw stones and eggs and she was injured in the attack. Trinamool Congress leaders have faced attacks, including eggs being thrown at them, after the BJP came to power in May 2026.

World.title: Har Ghar Tiranga rally teaching youngsters about sacrifices of freedom fighters: BJP MLA
World.content:
Etcherla BJP MLA N.Eswara Rao on Friday said that Har Ghar Tiranga rally enabled many youngsters to know about the great sacrifices of freedom fighters and inspired them to dedicate themselves to achieve Vikasit Bharat-20247 goals. On the eve of 80th Independence Day celebrations, he took out a major rally with national flags and covered over 30 villages of four mandals of Etcherla constituency of Srikakulam district.

Speaking to media on the occasion, he requested all students to read Indian freedom struggle history and biographies of great personalities of the country. Mr. Eswara Rao said that the Prime Minister Narendra Modi developed the country in the last 12 years and made every person to be a proud Indian. He said that villagers were requested to hoist their flag in their respective premises on August 15th and involve youngsters in the celebrations.

World.title: ‘Mining Bill a blow to Odisha’s fiscal autonomy’: BJD chief asks Majhi to convene all-party meet
World.content:
Former Chief Minister and Biju Janata Dal president Naveen Patnaik on Friday demanded a special session of the Assembly to voice dissent against the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which was passed by Parliament on Thursday. Mr. Patnaik said the Bill usurps Odisha’s fiscal autonomy and termed it a “threat” to the State’s constitutional rights over its resources.

In a letter to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Friday, the senior Opposition leader stated that provisions in the Bill would “disproportionately impact” mineral-rich States such as Odisha, leading to “massive revenue losses” and stifling the State’s developmental agenda.

A day earlier, hours after the Bill was cleared by the Rajya Sabha, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren had voiced criticism of the proposed legislation. He described it as a “black Bill” and warned of protests in “every district, every block, every panchayat, every town” of the State.

In his letter to Mr. Majhi, the BJD chief expressed concern at an amendment granting the sole authority over the framing of rules to the Centre and restricting States’ power to levy taxes on minerals.

“Odisha’s natural wealth belongs to her people, and the revenue generated from mining operations is crucial for financing healthcare, education, welfare schemes and infrastructure development across the State,” observed the former Chief Minister.

“By stripping the State of its power to impose taxes and cesses on its own mineral-bearing lands, the Union Government has dealt a heavy blow to federalism and State revenue autonomy,” he added and urged Mr. Majhi to immediately convene an all-party meeting.

World.title: Kochi Corporation Council approves proposal for new plant at Brahmapuram
World.content:
A proposal to establish a new plant at Brahmapuram with a capacity to treat 150 tonnes of biodegradable waste was passed through voting amid stiff protest from the Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) at the Kochi Corporation Council meeting on Friday (August 14).

The proposal, submitted by G3 Renewables Private Limited, which operates a facility on Willingdon Island, to set up the plant at an investment of ₹25–30 crore, provided the Corporation allots three acres on a 25-year lease, was included in the agenda. The plant proposes to employ proprietary mechanical processing technology recognised by the Suchitwa Mission.

The LDF opposed the agenda, following which it was put to vote and approved by 40 votes to 19, with BJP councillors also supporting the proposal. V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader, alleged that the agenda was being passed without the Mayor or the Corporation secretary having visited the Willingdon plant and without inviting expressions of interest (EoI). “The Council has been made to approve an agenda without knowing the finer points. The Mayor had no answer when asked whether Suchitwa Mission had examined the Willingdon facility. The compressed biogas plant already functional at Brahmapuram has failed to achieve its optimum capacity because of mixed waste being fed by the Corporation. Unless segregation is streamlined, the same problem will recur with the new plant,” he said.

Mayor V.K. Minimol countered that proposals must be vetted by the standing committee concerned, and that there was no precedent for the Mayor or the secretary to personally examine them. In this case, she said, the health standing committee had visited the plant. “We cannot afford to delay the proposed facility as nearly 100 tonnes of waste are now being dumped at Brahmapuram daily for want of adequate treatment capacity, with the CBG plant functioning far below its optimum. The company has agreed to transport waste from six primary collection points of the Corporation to the plant for a mere 20 paise per kilogram. This will substantially reduce lorry rent from the exorbitant ₹4.50 crore,” Ms. Minimol said, adding that an EoI would be invited.

Shortly thereafter, LDF councillors stormed the well of the council hall, accusing the Mayor of denying discussion on restricting subsidies for biomedical waste collection to eligible sections alone. Reasoning that the Opposition had already registered its protest when the matter was discussed in the health committee, Ms. Minimol left the dais, announcing that the Council agenda had been passed. Following this, Opposition councillors shifted their protest to the front of the Mayor’s chamber, even as she exited the Corporation office through another route.

World.title: ‘Ron Gowdru’ G.S. Patil unanimously elected Karnataka Assembly Speaker
World.content:
Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil, four-time Congress MLA from Ron in Gadag district, was unanimously elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. He is the 18th Speaker of the Assembly since 1972.

Popularly known as G.S. Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara.

From a political family

The 78-year-old Mr. Patil comes from an agrarian political family. His elder brother, R.S. Patil, was a former MP who represented the Bagalkot constituency, while another brother, B.S. Patil, served as Chief Secretary of Karnataka during the S.M. Krishna government. He contested eight Assembly elections and won four. Mr. B.S. Patil was present at the officers’ gallery in the House today.

A sportsperson, the newly elected Speaker was a wicketkeeper-batsman and played for the Mysore State team. He married Annapoorna in 1974 and has two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Prashanth, is a doctor, while his other son, Mithun, is a civil engineer.

More than a dozen members spoke on Mr. Patil’s elevation as Speaker, describing him as a person who has donned many hats with equal ease. Besides being a politician, he is a farmer, educationist, sportsperson and cooperative leader.

‘Police Patil’

Mr. Patil, whose extended family is popularly known as the “Police Patil” or “Ron Gowdru” family, is the chairman of the Rajiv Gandhi Educational Institutions and is associated with various organisations in Gadag district. He has also held several positions in the cooperative sector.

Former Minister H.K. Patil, MLA from Gadag, noted that prominent personalities such as Bharat Ratna awardee and Hindustani vocalist Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, classical musician Pandit Puttaraj Gawai and his father, K.H. Patil, hailed from Gadag district. Former Indian cricketer Sunil Joshi is also from the district.

Pro-tem Speaker T.B. Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Mr. Patil elected after a voice vote.

Amid thumping of desks by members, Mr. Shivakumar, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok, Mr. Jayachandra and Dr. Parameshwara accompanied Mr. Patil to the Speaker’s chair.

BJP boycotts

The BJP boycotted the election, protesting against the Congress high command’s decision to communicate Mr. Patil’s name on AICC letterhead. Mr. Ashok said the Speaker was elected by the Assembly and not the AICC, and appealed to Mr. Patil to discharge his duties impartially.

The post had fallen vacant following the resignation of U.T. Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3.

Perhaps for the first time, presiding officers of both Houses hail from north Karnataka.

World.title: PM Shehbaz briefs President Zardari on Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called on President Asif Ali Zardari in Islamabad on Friday and briefed him on a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, according to a statement issued by the Presidency.

For his part, President Zardari “expressed his best wishes for the effective implementation of the tripartite agreement with regard to defence cooperation, regional peace and stability and promotion of the security of the Muslim ummah”, the Presidency’s statement on its X account said.

He also appreciated PM Shehbaz’s and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts for “further strengthening the longstanding fraternal relations between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan into a robust strategic partnership”, the statement added.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 in Makkah, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia will form political and military mechanisms under the defence pact , Turkiye’s defence ministry said on Thursday, adding the alliance would also deepen defence industry cooperation.

Both Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Dar have said the pact is defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it is also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan.

Meanwhile, Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

Counter-terrorism also discussed

Apart from discussions on the Makkah pact, “the professional capabilities of the security forces and law enforcement agencies in operations against Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna al-Khawarij were appreciated” during Friday’s meeting, the statement by the Presidency said.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan, and Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

The meeting’s participants reiterated the “resolve to eradicate the scourge of terrorism” from the country, the statement said, adding that foreign and interior affairs were also discussed.

President Zardari also emphasised “the need for effective measures to provide relief to the people” in light of the current regional situation. He also stressed the need for “uninterrupted supply of essential commodities and their availability at reasonable prices”.

He “expressed the hope that Pakistan’s effective diplomatic efforts for the promotion of regional and global peace would further strengthen the country’s international standing, and that its positive impacts would be reflected in the national economy and the lives of the people”, the Presidency’s statement said.

The meeting was also attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Interior and Narcotics Control Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan and Senator Sherry Rehman.

World.title: Petroleum dealers postpone planned strike as govt approves margin revision
World.content:
The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers’ Association (PPDA) on Friday called off its plans to begin a strike on Saturday after the government approved a proposed revision in the dealers’ margins.

The nod for the revision was also confirmed by the finance ministry in a statement.

The Economic Coordination Committee had “deliberated on the matter regarding revision of dealers’ margins on motor spirit and high-speed diesel” during a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on a public holiday, the statement said, adding that a revision of the margin had been approved.

The statement did not specify the increase in the margin but a senior official told Dawn that the margin had been increased by Rs1.34.

The PPDA also said the government had increased the petroleum dealers’ margin by Rs1.34 per litre, bringing the total margin to around Rs10 per litre.

Following the increase, the dealers’ margin on both petrol and diesel will rise to Rs9.98 per litre from the existing Rs8.64 per litre.

As the PPDA Chairman Bakhsh announced during a press conference in Karachi that they were postponing the strike after the approval for the increase, he also said that petroleum product prices may once again be revised every 7 or 15 days, instead of being changed daily.

Last month, the government announced that it would start revising fuel prices on a daily basis, rather than the weekly system that had been in vogue in recent months. The government on Thursday rejected the dealers’ demand for monthly price fixing, adding that it will continue the daily price-fixing mechanism for petroleum products.

In its Friday statement, the PPDA said it “had postponed Saturday’s planned strike based on the government’s assurances”.

“However, [the PPDA chairman] warned that the association would continue its protest until all of its demands were accepted,” the statement added.

The association’s vice chairman, Tariq Hassan, further said that “because dealers had not received an increase in their margin for the past three years, approximately $50 million belonging to petroleum dealers remains outstanding with the government”.

On Wednesday, the PPDA issued a 72-hour ultimatum to the government over its failure to fulfil promises made by the petroleum minister to resolve their issues, especially the increase in margin to eight per cent on the retail sale price of petrol.

The association had warned that if the government failed to meet its demands within 72 hours, petrol pumps across the country would shut down indefinitely from 6am on Saturday (August 15) and would not reopen until those demands were met.

A delegation of petroleum dealers had also held brief talks with Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik in Islamabad on Wednesday.

In the meeting, the minister had assured the delegation that a Rs1.34 per litre increase in dealers’ margin, which had been pending for two years, had already been sent to the ECC and was awaiting approval from the Federal Cabinet.

Additional reporting by Mubarak Zeb Khan

World.title: World leaders extend greetings to Pakistan on Independence Day, hail bilateral ties
World.content:
Felicitations poured in from other nations on Friday as Pakistan celebrated 79 years of independence.

World leaders and diplomats, from the Iranian president to US State Secretary Marco Rubio, not just wished Pakistan and its people on the country’s 80th Independence Day, but also took the opportunity to hail Islamabad’s ties with their countries.

Saudi Arabia’s King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman congratulated President Asif Ali Zardari, wishing the government and people of Pakistan steady progress and prosperity, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

King Salman also praised the “strong relations” between the two countries, highlighting the “shared commitment to advancing cooperation across all fields”, SPA reported.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in a message to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, described Pakistan’s Independence Day as a valuable opportunity to honour the achievements of the nation, reaffirming Tehran’s firm resolve to further strengthen its relations with Pakistan, Iran’s IRNA news agency reported.

He also expressed “readiness to take more effective steps to advance bilateral ties” and “secure the common interests of both sides”, the report said.

It added that Pezeshkian noted that the “shared interests of the Iranian and Pakistani nations have become inextricably interwoven, a reality that underscores the need for greater synergy and closer cooperation” and stressed that a “new turning point has begun in deepening and expanding the longstanding and strategic relations” between Tehran and Islamabad.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi congratulated his Pakistani counterpart, Ishaq Dar, according to IRNA.

The state-run Iranian news agency reported that Araghchi said that continued political consultations and the strengthening of economic, trade, border, security, and cultural cooperation between the two countries would pave the way to leverage existing capacities and secure their shared interests.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in his message on Pakistan’s Independence Day, appreciated “the partnership between our nations and the bonds of friendship between our peoples”.

“Together, through our cooperation on regional mediation, critical minerals, energy, counterterrorism, cultural heritage, and trade and investment, we are turning potential into progress and delivering real results for Americans and Pakistanis alike,” Rubio said.

In Islamabad, US Chargé d’Affaires Natalie Baker met Dar and congratulated him.

Turkiye’s Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz also congratulated Pakistan and posted on X: “Our relations with Pakistan are based on an exceptional brotherhood nourished by our shared history, common values, and our determination to stand by each other in difficult times”.

He noted that the recent defence agreement between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had “added a new dimension” to relations between Ankara and Islamabad.

Turkiye’s foreign ministry also extended felicitations to the “friendly and brotherly Pakistan”.

Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, in a message to President Zardari, congratulated Pakistan on Independence Day, the Qatar News Agency reported.

Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a phone call with Dar and “extended warm greetings on Pakistan’s Independence Day to the leadership, government and people of Pakistan, and conveyed his best wishes for continued peace, progress and prosperity,” the FO said in another post.

Chinese ambassador to Pakistan, Jiang Zaidong, met Dar, congratulated him and reaffirmed the “close and time-tested ties between” Islamabad and China, according to the FO.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin congratulated President Zardari and PM Shehbaz, commending Pakistan-Russia relations.

“I am confident that we will continue our constructive joint efforts to further strengthen the entire spectrum of our partnership for the benefit of the friendly peoples of Russia and Pakistan, and in the interests of enhancing international security and stability,” a post on the Russian embassy’s X account quoted him as saying.

UK High Commissioner to Pakistan Jane Marriott, in a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, “conveyed warm wishes” on Pakistan’s Independence Day, the Foreign Office (FO) said on X.

Sultan of Oman Haitham bin Tarik and Kuwait’s Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Al Khaled Al Hamad Al Sabah congratulated Pakistan in their messages to President Zardari.

Somalia’s Foreign Ministry also extended congratulations to Pakistan.

In a post on X, the ministry said, “The Federal Republic of Somalia congratulates the government and people of Pakistan on their 79th Independence anniversary, reaffirming our commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation and friendship between our two nations”.

Romania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, in a statement posted on X, congratulated the Pakistani government and people, adding that “Romania remains committed to further strengthening our bilateral relations, including under the EU-Pakistan framework”.

Georgia, meanwhile, expressed its “cordial wishes for peace and prosperity of Pakistani people”, adding that it was looking forward to “further advancing our friendly relations”.

Azerbaijan also extended “heartfelt congratulations to the brotherly people and the government of Pakistan”.

World.title: 2 suspects in fatal attacks on Lahore cops killed in Muridke fire exchange, say police
World.content:
LAHORE: Two men who allegedly shot dead three police officials in Lahore on Thursday were killed during an exchange of fire with law enforcers at a house in Muridke where they had held a family hostage, police sources told Dawn.

Police officials identified the suspects as a father-son duo, Fayyaz Butt and Rehan Butt, saying that they were killed in a joint operation by Lahore police, Counter-Terrrorism Department (CTD) personnel, Sheikhpura police and Elite Force personnel on Friday morning after an hours-long chase from Lahore to Muridke.

The suspects held the driver of a Lahore Waste Management Company vehicle at gunpoint and forced him to keep on driving to reach Muridke, the officials said.

According to police, they allegedly shot dead two policemen in Lahore’s Badami Bagh area and one at Yateem Khana Chowk, Multan Road, besides injuring three on Thursday night.

Initial police inquiries showed that the first armed attack was carried out by Rehan and his accomplices in Badami Bagh. The martyred officials were identified as Sub-Inspector (SI) Adeel Ashiq and Constable Asad.

An hour later, the suspects allegedly targeted policemen deployed at the headquarters of the banned Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) on Multan Road and opened indiscriminate firing.

On Friday, a senior official who coordinated the joint operation against the suspects told Dawn a third suspect, identified as Tariq, managed to flee. His last location was reported as Bagh in Azad Jammu Kashmir (AJK).

AJK police and the law enforcement agencies from Punjab were working to trace and arrest him, he said.

Regarding Friday’s operation, the official said Fayyaz and Rehan were traced to a seminary in Muridke. Law enforcers surrounded it after reaching the site while the seminary’s management claimed that the two were not present there.

To verify the claim, police seized the seminary’s DVR, but found that the cameras were not working, he said, adding that the DVR was sent to Lahore for forensic analysis.

Meanwhile, law enforcers received information that the suspects had gone toward River Ravi and were hiding in a forest, the official said.

On the directions of IG police Punjab Abdul Kareem, the police used thermal drones to trace the suspects in the forest, he said, adding that the suspects moved to a densely populated area as they realised they were being traced.

“They barged into a house, took the family hostage and threatened to kill them,” he said, adding that the suspects opened fire on the police personnel when they reached there. During the exchange of fire, Rehan and Fayyaz were killed, he said.

He said Tariq had separated from them and fled to AJK during the chase.

After Thursday’s attack, a police official had told Dawn that the incidents seemed to be an act of revenge. Rehan’s brother, Faizan Butt, was allegedly killed in an encounter with a CTD team, which reportedly included SI Adeel, a few years back, the official said.

Faizan was reportedly working for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and he was involved in the killing of some police officials, the police official said. He added that SI Adeel had told police higher-ups in 2024 that he was receiving life threats from Rehan.

Following his complaint, a first information report was registered against Rehan in November 2024 with Shafiqabad police. According to the FIR, Adeel had alleged that he had received a WhatsApp call from Rehan, who had threatened to kill him.

World.title: Nadra launches locally made QR code-based identity cards
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) on Wednesday launched a new chipless National Identity Card (NIC) built around a secure QR code, replacing the imported microchip used for the past 14 years.

The card has been manufactured domestically by the National Security Printing Company (NSPC) in Karachi in line with Nadra’s technical and security specifications, a statement issued by the authority on Friday said.

Instead of a chip, the card will carry a secure QR code that can be scanned and verified on a smartphone through Nadra’s Pak Identity (PakID) mobile application, it added.

The federal government approved the issuance of the new card on February 23 this year.

The code will contain the cardholder’s information and photograph.

According to Nadra, this will allow institutions to enter individuals’ names, addresses and other identity details more easily and consistently in their systems while reducing data entry errors.

The card will also display a family number and symbols to denote persons with disabilities, senior citizens, organ donors and citizens of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The cardholder’s name and address will be printed in both Urdu and English, Nadra added.

The visible and covert security features of the card have been “updated to meet current requirements and align with domestic manufacturing capabilities”, the statement said.

Nadra said the chip-based Smart NIC introduced about 14 years ago could not be fully utilised as chip readers and supporting infrastructure were never widely available. The QR-based card addresses this gap, being verifiable through an ordinary smartphone or software connected to a camera, it said.

Telecom operators, banks, hospitals, the Pakistan Railways, police and other authorised institutions will also be provided with software to read and verify the QR code, Nadra said.

The rollout will be phased, with the QR code-based card replacing the standard CNIC from Friday, it said, adding that from January 2027, it will be issued for all categories, including NICs for Overseas Pakistanis (Nicops) and Juvenile Cards. In the final phase, the Pakistan Origin Card (POC) will also transition to the chipless format, according to the statement.

Nadra clarified that all previously issued identity cards would remain valid until their expiry dates.

In February, the government notified amendments to the National Identity Card Rules, 2002 and the Pakistan Origin Card Rules, 2002 to modernise the country’s identity document framework. Part of these reforms included the statutory introduction of the QR code — a scannable barcode containing horizontal and vertical lines, dots, and patterns — as a defined security and verification feature.

The amendments further authorised the use of a QR code or “any other technological feature”, in lieu of the current microchip, enabling Nadra to adopt evolving verification technologies without repeated rule amendments.

World.title: Balochistan home minister unhurt as convoy comes under attack in Mastung
World.content:
QUETTA: Six people, including three police personnel, were injured in an armed attack on the convoy of Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove in Mastung on Friday.

A senior police official told Dawn that the home minister remained unhurt in the attack, which occurred as his convoy reached the Khad Kocha area of Mastung. He said that Langove was on his way to Quetta from Kalat.

The official added that six people sustained bullet injuries in the attack, three of whom were police personnel.

Nawab Raisani Memorial Hospital’s Dr Sana also confirmed to Dawn that six injured had been brought to the hospital and two of them were in serious condition. She said two of the others were referred to Quetta.

Security forces have cordoned off the area and launched a search operation.

Langove, who is from the Balochistan Awami Party, was sworn in as provincial home minister in March.

Langove had also served as the provincial home minister previously, but his appointment was declared null and void after he was de-notified on August 21, 2024.

World.title: Afghan soil being used against Pakistan, Naqvi tells Norway FM as two discuss counterterrorism cooperation
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday met with Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, where the two sides discussed counterterrorism cooperation, particularly the use of Afghan soil in terror attacks against Pakistan.

Eide arrived in Pakistan a day earlier on a two-day visit — the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade.

According to a handout issued by the interior ministry, the two leaders discussed strengthening bilateral relations and the regional situation. Naqvi and Eide also agreed to improve cooperation in counterterrorism, prevention of illegal immigration, police training, and mutual legal assistance.

The two sides held discussions on the situation in neighbouring Afghanistan and the activities of proscribed organisations operating from the neighbouring country.

During the meeting, Eide lauded Pakistan’s “constructive and active” role in the US-Iran war. The two sides also discussed measures taken against illegal immigration to Europe from Pakistan.

“Pakistan’s effective measures have led to a 47 per cent reduction in illegal immigration to Europe,” the statement quoted Naqvi as saying, adding that “a zero-tolerance policy has been adopted against illegal immigration”.

He said that Pakistan’s measures against illegal immigration were also appreciated by the European Union.

“Promoting legal immigration is very important for effectively curbing illegal immigration,” he said.

According to the statement, Naqvi told Eide that “Afghan soil is continuously being used for terrorism in Pakistan” and that Pakistan stood “as a wall” between the world and terrorist elements.

“Everyone must work together for the complete eradication of terrorism.” Naqvi was quoted as saying. He also told Eide that his visit would be an “important milestone” in strengthening bilateral relations between Norway and Pakistan.
